That is the opportunism. Guilt is not heritable. Charles was born in 1948. The men and women who captained the ships, bought the captives and worked the estates are dust. So are the African kings who captured them. The Kingdom of Dahomey ran a militarised slave economy and sold prisoners of war down to the coast at Ouidah for generations; Britain had to force it to stop in the 1850s. The Ashanti empire’s wealth rested on gold and slaves. Oyo, the coastal middlemen, the traders of the interior: the transatlantic trade did not begin when a European ship appeared on the horizon. It began when an African polity decided a neighbour was stock. The Arab and Muslim trade out of East Africa and across the Sahara ran longer and, on several serious counts, took more people. Nobody is invoicing Riyadh, Istanbul or the successors of Dahomey. The invoice is always presented in London, because London still pays, still feels awkward, and still has a public class that treats national self-accusation as a moral personality.

Britain’s actual record is the one the campaign has to blur. Parliament outlawed the British slave trade in 1807. It abolished slavery across most of the empire in 1833, freeing more than 760,000 people, and it paid the owners about £20 million to get the bill through. That sum was around 40 per cent of annual government expenditure and about 5 per cent of national output. Part of it was financed by undated gilts that were finally redeemed in 2015, which reparations lobbyists now wave as if the British public had been paying slave owners a secret stipend for 180 years. They were paying off a debt raised to end the institution. After 1807 the Royal Navy’s West Africa Squadron spent half a century intercepting the trade Britain had just made illegal for its own subjects. It took about 1,600 ships and freed about 150,000 Africans. Somewhere around 1,500 to 1,600 British sailors died on that station, mostly of disease. At its height the patrol cost on the order of 2 per cent of GDP. Portugal and Britain between them shipped more than 70 per cent of the transatlantic total, and Portugal shipped the larger share for long stretches. Spain kept the trade going later. The United States abolished slavery in 1865, by war. Britain did it by Act of Parliament, by cheque, and by naval blockade, earlier than almost anyone else with an empire. That is not the behaviour of a state that has a moral debt still outstanding in 2026. It is the behaviour of the state that closed the trade down and made other people hate it for doing so.

The legal trick is as cynical as the number. Slavery in the British Caribbean was lawful under the law of the time. International law did not then forbid it. A petition that asks a court in 2026 to declare an eighteenth-century statute a crime, and then to invent a duty to pay, is not jurisprudence. It is politics with a wig on. Jamaica cannot sue Britain at the International Court of Justice, which is why the route chosen is the Privy Council, a court that still exists because these same states have not yet cut the last constitutional string. They want the King as head of state to refer a case whose purpose is to extract money from the country of which he is also King. If he apologises in a formal, governmental sense, every lawyer on the circuit will treat the apology as an admission. That is why the apology is the point. Regret is free. An apology is a pleading.

The wider demands give the game away. CARICOM’s menu is not confined to a historical accounting. It includes debt cancellation, development assistance, healthcare funding and what they call decolonisation. Debt cancellation for loans taken out by independent governments in the late twentieth century has nothing to do with a barracoon in 1720. Healthcare funding is a budget bid. “Decolonisation” means republicanism, the removal of the Privy Council, and the symbolic humiliation of the Crown, after which the cash demand will still be there. Several of these countries have been independent for sixty years. Their murder rates, their governance failures, their emigration to the very country they are invoicing, are present-tense facts. Britain’s aid budgets, remittances from the British diaspora, and the open door of the NHS and the universities have transferred more wealth west-to-east since independence than the slave trade ever did in the other direction. None of that appears on the invoice.

This is the same caper the left, the Britain-haters and the woke have run for years, merely franchised. Take a real historical evil. Erase every actor who is not European. Erase the abolitionists, the sailors, the £20 million, the Squadron. Inflate a consultancy model until the number is too big to mean anything. Then present the refusal to pay as proof of ongoing guilt. At home the same people use it to indict the country that abolished the trade. Abroad, elites who cannot fix their own police forces, their own debts or their own schools get a permanent alibi and a claim on someone else’s treasury. The Commonwealth is treated not as a voluntary association but as a claims department.

The Palace has, for once, refused to play. The government, even this pathetic government, has said it will not pay and will not apologise. That is the correct answer, and it should be the last one. No formal apology. No referral that can be spun as an admission. No “non-cash reparatory justice” that turns into cash the moment the communiqué is signed. No seat at a table whose only agenda item is a bill for the dead, presented to people who were not alive, by governments that will not ask the same question of anyone else. The past was brutal. Britain ended its part in it at vast cost, in treasure and in lives, and then spent decades stopping other people from continuing it. That is the record. The rest is a caper.

text:
Sony Thang’s posts are rhetoric, not analysis. The method is the problem.
He treats every U.S. action as one pattern and every Chinese outcome as outside that pattern. Xinjiang, Taiwan, Tibet, the South China Sea, and the property bust never have to be explained. Washington calling China a threat is offered as proof China is not one. That is circular. States arm against rivals they trade with. The U.S. sold grain to the USSR and still contained it.
“America fell, China only held the mirror” skips the numbers. U.S. GDP is about $32 trillion to China’s $21 trillion. Output per person is roughly $90,000 versus $15,000. Unemployment is in the mid-4 percent range here. China’s home prices have fallen for about 37 straight months, property investment is down about 19 percent, youth unemployment is near 15 percent, and public debt including local financing vehicles is around 124 percent of GDP. A country in that shape is not the verdict on American decline.
The socialism point is missing entirely. China’s catch-up started when Deng dropped the command economy, not when the Party perfected it. Private firms, foreign capital, and export markets did the growing. The Party kept the banks, the land, and the political monopoly. Those are the parts now failing.
A list of U.S. interventions is not a theory of why Chinese households stopped spending, or why the dollar still clears the world’s trade.

في سوسيولوجيا الدين تمثل الماركسية ديانة علمانية وحسب الفيلسوف الابستمولوجي "كارل بوبر" أنها عقيدة دوغمائية وعلم زائف، نفس النتيجة عند فيلسوف العلم "ماريو بونجي" وعالم الاقتصاد "توماس سويل" الذي كان ماركسيا سابقا. في هذه الحلقة من دروس "Open College" التي يقدمها الحداثي الليبرالي "ستيفن هيكس" وأبرز نقاد الماركسية وما بعد الحداثة، نتعرف إلى السر الذي ما زال يجعل الاشتراكية تجذب أتباعًا بعد أكثر من قرن على دعوة كارل ماركس وفريدريك إنجلز للثورة الشيوعية عام 1848.

كان من أوائل مؤيدي الاشتراكية رجال دين، كالرهبان والراهبات على سبيل المثال. لكن ماركس وإنجلز قدّما ما أسمياه الاشتراكية العلمية. ومع ذلك، عند النظر إلى كتاباتهما، يتبادر إلى الذهن سؤال: هل هي حقًا قائمة على الحقائق والأدلة والحجج والتجارب، وعلى كامل منظومة العقل؟ أم أنها في نهاية المطاف نوع من الالتزام الإيماني؟

في النهاية، يُشبّه الدكتور هيكس رؤاهما المثالية بجنة عدن حديثة، ملحدة. ستيفن آر. سي. هيكس، الحاصل على درجة الدكتوراه، هو أستاذ الفلسفة في جامعة روكفورد بالولايات المتحدة الأمريكية، وقد شغل مناصب زائرة في جامعة جورج تاون في واشنطن العاصمة، وجامعة كازيمير العظيم في بولندا، وكلية هاريس مانشستر التابعة لجامعة أكسفورد في إنجلترا، وجامعة ياغيلونيا في بولندا.

- Socialism continues to attract followers more than a century after Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels first called for communist revolution in 1848.  Dr. Hicks sets out to investigate what is the attraction.

Early adherents of socialism were religious: monks and nuns, for instance.  But Marx and Engels offered what they called scientific socialism.  And yet, when you look at their writings, one has to ask: is it really based on facts, evidence, argumentation, experimentation, the whole apparatus of reason? Or is it ultimately a kind of faith commitment? 

In the end, Dr. Hicks likens their idealistic visions to a modernized, atheistic Garden of Eden.

For some time, Professor Hicks has been doing a philosophical analysis podcast on a wide range of contemporary topics.  It has been available on a number of other platforms.  It is now being offered on YouTube as well.  Its mission is to “ to explain the chaos.”

Stephen R. C. Hicks, Ph.D., is Professor of Philosophy at Rockford University, USA, and has had visiting positions at Georgetown University in Washington, D.C., University of Kasimir the Great in Poland, Oxford University’s Harris Manchester College in England, and Jagiellonian University in Poland.

text:
🇸🇻 THIS WEEK IN EL SALVADOR | VOL. 15
⠀
SEPTEMBER 26 – OCTOBER 3, 2026
⠀
A WEEK OF ECONOMIC MOMENTUM
⠀
5.1% economic growth. A stock market up 38.6%. IMF approval. Construction financing exceeding $1.62 billion. Growing exports. International tourism recognition.
⠀
And in the heart of San Salvador, a historic tribute to the man who dreamed of a united Central America.
⠀
This week brought together economic results, international confidence, investment, innovation, security and national history.
⠀
Here are the developments shaping El Salvador.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
1. THE IMF APPROVES $138 MILLION AS EL SALVADOR'S ECONOMY EXCEEDS EXPECTATIONS
⠀
One of the week's most significant announcements came from Washington.
⠀
On October 1, the International Monetary Fund's Executive Board completed the second and third reviews of its financing arrangement with El Salvador, allowing an immediate disbursement of approximately $138 million.
⠀
The IMF reported that economic activity had exceeded expectations, supported by sustained improvements in security and growing investor confidence.
⠀
It also recognized progress in fiscal consolidation, financial resilience and the strengthening of liquidity and reserve buffers.
⠀
The approval represents an important milestone in El Salvador's $1.4 billion financing arrangement.
⠀
For international investors, the IMF's assessment provides another reference point when evaluating the country's economic direction.
⠀
The bigger story is the convergence of stronger economic performance, international financing and growing investment interest.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
2. EL SALVADOR'S ECONOMY GROWS 5.1%
⠀
The Central Reserve Bank reported that El Salvador's economy expanded 5.1% during the second quarter of 2026.
⠀
That compares with 4.1% growth during the corresponding period of 2025.
⠀
Construction, healthcare and electricity were among the principal drivers.
⠀
A separate economic activity indicator showed growth of 4.5% in July, with construction continuing to make an important contribution.
⠀
These figures help explain why the construction industry has become one of the central stories in our recent weekly editions.
⠀
Investment is increasingly visible in the country's economic indicators and its changing urban landscape.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
3. EL SALVADOR'S STOCK MARKET SURGES 38.6%
⠀
Another major financial indicator arrived this week.
⠀
According to figures published by the Financial System Superintendency, trading activity on the Salvadoran stock exchange reached $4.483 billion between January and August 2026.
⠀
That represents an increase of 38.6% compared with the same period in 2025.
⠀
The market registered 4,827 transactions during those eight months.
⠀
International securities transactions accounted for approximately $1.449 billion, while investment funds reported total assets of approximately $2.216 billion.
⠀
Meanwhile, the integrated stock market connecting El Salvador and Panama recorded $165.3 million in transactions.
⠀
These figures illustrate the increasing activity and regional connections of El Salvador's capital markets.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
4. CONSTRUCTION FINANCING EXCEEDS $1.62 BILLION
⠀
The country's construction expansion is also reflected in bank lending.
⠀
Loans associated with construction exceeded $1.62 billion through August.
⠀
Housing, land development and commercial infrastructure accounted for approximately 97% of that financing portfolio.
⠀
Another indicator reinforces the picture.
⠀
Construction-related imports surpassed $1.13 billion during the first eight months of 2026.
⠀
The relationship between financing and material imports helps illustrate the scale of activity underway.
⠀
Following last week's announcements involving Paseo Vivo, Reforma 150 and San Benito 53, these figures provide broader economic context for the projects transforming metropolitan San Salvador and other parts of the country.
⠀
@LRodriguez_SV, Executive Director of the San Salvador Metropolitan Area Planning Office (@COAMSS_OPAMSS), has been highlighting the investment momentum behind this construction expansion. His involvement in the recently announced Paseo Vivo development in Apopa illustrates how the institution is helping facilitate new projects and attract investment to areas benefiting from improved security conditions.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
5. BUSINESS DELEGATIONS FROM 21 COUNTRIES EXPLORE EL SALVADOR
⠀
El Salvador's economic diplomacy continues opening international doors.
⠀
According to reporting published this week, business delegations representing 21 countries have visited El Salvador to explore commercial and investment opportunities.
⠀
The initiative reflects an international outreach strategy focused on attracting businesses, expanding commercial relationships and presenting opportunities in the Salvadoran market.
⠀
Combined with the latest economic results and IMF developments, these international contacts form another part of the country's investment story.
⠀
The challenge ahead is converting business interest into completed investments, jobs and long-term economic activity.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
6. EXPORTS REACH $4.529 BILLION
⠀
El Salvador exported approximately $4.529 billion in goods between January and August 2026.
⠀
Central America and the United States remained its principal commercial partners, together accounting for 81.1% of total exports.
⠀
Food products were identified as one of the most dynamic export categories.
⠀
Another report highlighted El Salvador's regional performance in export sophistication, reflecting the ability of Salvadoran companies to manufacture and commercialize increasingly diversified products.
⠀
The importance extends beyond total export values.
⠀
Industrial capabilities, product development and access to international markets help determine how Salvadoran businesses can compete and expand.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
7. WORLD TOURISM DAY COMES TO EL SALVADOR
⠀
El Salvador hosted World Tourism Day 2026, marking the first time the country welcomed this international event organized under the United Nations tourism framework.
⠀
Tourism Minister @MorenaValdezSV highlighted the country's international recognition for tourism growth.
⠀
Figures reported during the week placed El Salvador's tourism growth at approximately 37% during the referenced reporting period.
⠀
The international event provided an opportunity to present El Salvador's destinations, tourism development and growing international visibility.
⠀
Tourism also connects directly with other recurring themes in our reports: security, aviation, hospitality investment, infrastructure and employment.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
8. FRANCISCO MORAZÁN: HONORING A DREAM OF CENTRAL AMERICAN UNITY
⠀
October 3 marked the 234th anniversary of the birth of General Francisco Morazán.
⠀
This year's commemoration carried special historical significance.
⠀
For the first time, the ceremony took place at his newly inaugurated mausoleum in Jardín Centroamérica, beside the National Palace in San Salvador.
⠀
Government officials, members of the diplomatic corps, military personnel and citizens participated in the commemorative activities.
⠀
The ceremony included military honors, cannon salutes, a floral offering, the Salvadoran national anthem and an aerial display.
⠀
Defense Minister @merino_monroy emphasized Morazán's commitment to a cause that extended beyond national borders: Central American unity.
⠀
The new mausoleum, inaugurated following President @nayibbukele's initiative, places Morazán's remains in the heart of San Salvador's revitalized Historic Center.
⠀
It also creates a public space dedicated to remembering his life and political ideals.
⠀
More than a historical monument, the new mausoleum offers future generations an opportunity to discover the story of a leader who devoted his life to the vision of a united Central America.
⠀
His dream remains an important part of the region's shared history.
⠀
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
⠀
9. OCTOBER BEGINS WITH TWO HOMICIDE-FREE DAYS
⠀
El Salvador entered October with two consecutive days without homicides, according to figures released by the National Civil Police.
⠀
October 1 and October 2 were both reported as homicide-free.
⠀
The official figures brought the country's accumulated total to 235 homicide-free days during 2026 through October 2.
⠀

text:
Travel pool report #4: Rally departure

POTUS took the stage at 7:45 pm to a standing ovation. He ended at 9:17 pm with the “YMCA” dance.

Some highlights for you to check against transcripts:

- The president again asked people to pretend he is on the ballot: “I’m really in to win it. We want to win the midterm … If you don’t mind please pretend that I’m on the ballot.”

- People stood up and cheered when he offered $5000 checks if Republicans keep control of Congress. Near the end of the rally he brought it up again, and several people clapped and jumped up and down.

- A protester was escorted out shortly after the president began talking.

- There was thunderous applause for a Voter ID measure on the Ohio ballot; for POTUS saying that zero undocumented immigrants have been admitted across the border; and for his support for barring transgender people from women’s sports.

- John Husted got applause when the president highlighted his attempts to get legislation passed that the president said would stop data centers from driving up utility costs.

- People began streaming out from an upper deck and seats along the side of the auditorium once the speech hit the 45-minute mark. Around that point, the president read the poem The Snake and dedicated it to the town of Springfield Ohio

- He pondered the future: “I’ll try a couple of years of being nonconsequential if you don’t mind. This is a dangerous position.”

- “I had a simple life before this. He said that he didn’t have to be here on a Saturday night“working my ass off.” “I could’ve been in Monte Carlo!” At that, the president received a standing ovation and a “four more years” chat. He said he’d “like to do that” but then complained that the news media would report that he wanted to run again.

- He disparaged polls showing dimming prospects for Republicans as fake, and said the polls have not taken into account the fact that he is now campaigning. “It’s their fault because they’ve unleashed us.”

- He invited Husted onstage. Husted got a standing ovation when he said this week Ohio reported the lowest unemployment rate in the history of Ohio.

- He invited Ramaswamy onstage, and he said he was running against the “Kamala Harris of Ohio.” His challenger’s name is Amy Acton. The president called her a “radical left lunatic.”

- The president thanked Bill Pulte for attending and someone in the crowd yelled out “Wild Bill Pulte!”

- He said “the Golden Age is upon us but you must get out and vote Republican.”

- He seemed happy to see “Mr Wall” of his diehard Front Row Joes fan club. He said “in my final appearance I’m going to put a jacket on like that,” gesturing to the man’s brick wall-print suit.

Also of note: The president’s motorcade was rerouted to the venue initially due to the protest outside, per a USSS official.

Thanks to Haley Bull & Elyse Perlmutter for catching a few of these things.

Pool was ushered out while the president was still onstage and interacting with fans behind him.

Rolling to airport at 9:23 pm.

Katie Rogers
The New York Times
Sat. Oct. 3, 9:27 PM

On October 3, former Yokozuna Hakuho took part in harvesting sake rice in Gokokuji-machi, Komatsu City. Under the watchful eye of Naohiko Noguchi, who is recognized as a holder of Ishikawa Prefecture's Intangible Cultural Heritage for Sake Brewing Master, Hakuho worked alongside local residents, expressing his hopes: "It is a joy to be involved in sake making with Mr. Noguchi, whom I have respected since my active days. I hope a delicious sake comes out of this."

At the rice paddy where he had participated in rice planting in late April, Hakuho held a sickle and harvested stalks of "Yamada Nishiki" rice one after another. Receiving advice from local farmers, he also operated a combine harvester to bring in the harvest across an area of approximately 1,000 square meters.

Speaking to reporters after the harvest, Hakuho commented on Yokozuna Onosato, who secured his first tournament victory in a year at the Aki Basho: "Only the wrestler himself understands the fight against injury, but I think he fought very hard." Regarding his former disciple Enho, who narrowly ended up with a losing record in the Juryo division, he offered words of encouragement: "It was unfortunate, but I hope he bounces back in the next tournament."

text:
In fall of 2008 I was a student at Texas Tech. If you recall, until recently, that was our best football season in decades. Harrell. Crabtree. The Catch. An amazing experience. Took down number 1 University of Texas. 

A week later, Tech took down (I think #9) Oklahoma State. 

Soon after, Tech went to Norman and…well, we were embarrassed. We were so close. And one game broke us. I hated it. Was up in arms all night, going through the five stages of grief. My team pooped the bed. Not good. Shut down the party. It was difficult to sleep that evening. 

Then, a little perspective hit. We had a historic season that was not over. And I was letting a bunch of 18-23 year olds dictate my mood based on what they did in another state. No one died. Bummed? Sure. But this is not defcon 5, and getting so worked up over this would not bring any balance to the equation. As soon as I realized this, I’ve slept comfortably. (And as a tech fan this philosophy got me through 2015-2023.)

@dctf does it best. They are historic. They are better than espn in every way. They bring us Texas sports every single day. Don’t tell my boss, but I enjoy watching @Tepper every week during work. @Matt_Stepp817 is the go-to for breaking sport news in my opinion. One mess up on their app rollout does not take that away. Not only that, but unlike most companies they are listening to their audience and course correcting. Good for them. If you can, subscribe to their services because what they do is powerful. If you can’t, don’t, and enjoy the free version. 

They are not paying us or asking us to say this. As we travel the state we simply notice what they offer and it’s real and it’s a beautiful way to honor the competitive youth in our state. Good on Dave Campbells.

text:
Well, well, well;

We know now why the U.S. Attorney's Office in Boston was up for 30 hours straight, and why they filed a motion on Saturday night before trial at 9PM ET;

Here's the categories of material the DOJ may now have from Matthew Farwell's phone as to Sandra Birchmore's death;

"[W]eb searches, contact list, his photos and videos, health data, step count, GPS and other location evidence, text messages with others leading up to and following Ms. Birchmore’s death, as well as his call history."

Source page 7-8 = https://t.co/F0K0Zex3P4

Later in the document, the DOJ notes;

"Despite the defendant’s efforts to delete data, in the hours since the defendant announced he now consents to a full search, the government has identified incriminating evidence on that device. The government intends to introduce several artifacts from that device at trial. Any objections related to late notice should be waived. With the exception of the time it took MSP to quickly image his device on February 9, 2021, the defendant has had access to the original device and his counsel has had access to the forensic image of the phone since October 1, 2024. Given that the government did not have lawful authority to access the image of that phone until October 2, 2026, any objections based on notice should be deemed waived."

Source page 10 = https://t.co/F0K0Zex3P4

In short, Farwell's lawyers attempted to introduce evidence from Farwell's phone that Farwell blocked Sandra's number on February 3, 2021.

However, the US DOJ, via U.S. Attorney Leah Foley's office, then countered in open court with a shocking revelation.

As the DOJ explains;

"On October 2, 2026, four days before jury selection, to the government’s surprise, an attorney for the defendant announced in open court that on February 9, 2021, the defendant consented to a full search of his phone for all evidence related to the death of Sandra Birchmore.3  When the Court inquired, Farwell’s counsel stated unequivocally that it was her position that Farwell consented to the full search in February 2021 and that the government still had legal authority to search Farwell’s phone for evidence of Ms. Birchmore’s death, except in any communications that Farwell had with his wife or counsel.

"When the government objected to Farwell’s misstatement of the facts, the Court inquired about defense counsel intent to use the defendant’s alleged consent in opening statements. Another attorney for the defendant then indicated that the defense may tell the jury that Farwell’s consent was not limited solely to the communications between himself and Ms. Birchmore, but would track the language on the consent form. However, that is the problem. Such a statement would be at odds with the recorded interview of Sgt. Fanning, the interview of Trooper Guarino, and extraction parameters of Trooper Guarino applied. Counsel indicated that the defense would confine its argument to the language of the document, presumably Exhibit A, which is inadmissible both because it is hearsay and because it is misleading. A statement of consent may, in certain circumstances, be a non-hearsay verbal act. United States v. Mena, 863 F.2d 1522, 1531 (11th Cir. 1989). However here, the consent was actually more limited than what was written in the form, rendering it hearsay because the defendant’s verbal consent, and not the form itself, had the legal effect.

"Had the defendant’s recent announcement been true, members of local law enforcement would have been able to search the defendant’s iPhone 11 for his web searches, contact list, his photos and videos, health data, step count, GPS and other location evidence, text messages with others leading up to and following Ms. Birchmore’s death, as well as his call history. The defendant offers no theory for why, despite allegedly providing full consent, investigators only searched the small fraction of his phone that could contain messages with Birchmore: messages that he, by all accounts, deleted in advance of his meeting with investigators."

Source page 6-8 = https://t.co/F0K0Zex3P4

For more context on the tragic death of Sandra Birchmore and her unborn 8-10 week old baby boy, earlier Saturday I reported;

New motion up on the Matthew Farwell and Sandra Birchmore docket just now from U.S. Attorney Leah Foley's office.

Summary;

The United States has filed a motion in limine in United States v. Matthew Farwell (D. Mass., No. 24-10259-DJC) asking the court to stop the defense from mischaracterizing the scope of Farwell’s February 9, 2021 consent to a search of his iPhone 11.

The motion seeks four limits:

Barring argument that Farwell consented to a full search of the phone on February 9, 2021.

Barring cross-examination of law enforcement about failing to search the phone based on any consent given before October 2, 2026.

Barring use of the written consent form (or similar self-serving statements) as evidence unless Farwell testifies.

Deeming waived any late-notice objections to exhibits generated from the October 2, 2026 search.

Background as alleged by the government;

Sandra Birchmore was found dead in her Canton apartment on February 4, 2021, seated partly under a closet doorknob with a ligature around her neck. On February 6, investigators identified Farwell on surveillance video entering her apartment around 9:14 p.m. and leaving around 9:43 p.m., masked and hooded. He told investigators he had deleted all communications with her and was allowed to keep his iPhone 11 for three more days.

On February 9, 2021, he and his lawyer met Massachusetts State Police Sgt. John Fanning and signed a form that referred to items “related to the death suicide of Sandra Birchmore.” The government says Farwell orally limited that consent to “conversations with Sandra,” which he had already deleted. The same day he searched, on his department phone, whether Cellebrite could recover deleted iMessages. 

Trooper Nicholas Guarino extracted the phone but reviewed only messages between Farwell and Birchmore, found none, and returned the device. 

A March 10, 2021 letter from Farwell’s attorney described the download as limited to “certain information.”

The government says this limited-consent understanding held through years of litigation (including a 2024 filter-team production of the forensic image --with an assurance the prosecution team had not reviewed it-- an April 2026 detention hearing, and a September 2026 filing) until October 2, 2026, the Friday before jury empanelment, when defense counsel asserted in open court that Farwell had consented to a full search related to Birchmore’s death (except communications with his wife or counsel).

Arguments;

The government contends that telling the jury the consent tracked the form would be false and misleading under Rule 403, inconsistent with Fanning’s and Guarino’s accounts and with the extraction that was actually performed. It treats the form as inadmissible self-serving hearsay rather than a verbal act, because the operative consent was the narrower oral limit. 

It also argues that cross-examining agents for not searching data they lacked authority to review would be improper, citing United States v. Collins, 409 F. Supp. 3d 228 (S.D.N.Y. 2019). 

Finally, it says any notice objections to newly identified artifacts should be waived: the defense has had the image since October 2024, while the government says it gained lawful authority to review the rest of the data only on October 2, 2026, and has since found incriminating evidence despite Farwell’s deletions.

The motion asks the court to rule before openings or voir dire so the claimed prejudice cannot be cured by a later objection.

On August 24th, 2024, Brian Tully, John Fanning and Nick Guarino's State Police Unit "lost" the entire server upon which Sandra Birchmore's laptop data was located within the Norfolk DA's SPDU unit.

That "data loss" occurred just four days before Farwell's arrest on federal charges, and just nine days after Tully and Fanning were made aware (via a meeting with the state medical examiner, the FBI and the US Attorney's office) that Farwell would soon be arrested on federal charges.

Interestingly, in October of 2024, Nick Guarino was then hit by a drunk driver on the Mass Pike during a detail (no charges resulted from the crime but Guarino is now a cooperating federal witness against Farwell).

A motion from Farwell's lawyers, related to Nick Guarino admitting to that data loss during a 2026 interview with the FBI, is expected to hit the docket before Monday, October 5th, 2026.

Farwell, also, for the first time, consented to a full search of his phone for all data related to Sandra's death.

John Fanning, another state trooper working for Tully's unit, told the FBI during formal interrogation that Fanning "told Guarino Farwell only consented to a search of his phone for messages between Sandra and Farwell, and that they were all deleted," however, now, Fanning tells the FBI Fanning "may have been mistaken."

As a result, Farwell's lawyers then provided the US DOJ consent to search Farwell's entire phone, following a question on the record in open court from Chief Judge Denise J. Casper.

Judge Casper expects jury selection to begin Tuesday, October 6th, 2026, and opening statements are expected on Friday October 9, 2026.

Each side will have 40 minutes for openings.

Farwell, alleges the DOJ , killed Sandra on February 1, 2021, and then, over the course of that year, covered up the crime with the help of Tully, Fanning and the rest of Norfolk DA's Michael Morrissey's men.

That was until August of 2023, through August of 2024, at which point the FBI exposed the cover up and, on August 28th, 2024, Farwell was federally indicted for Sandra's murder.

In the fall of 2025, a new law signed by President Trump (@POTUS) was also used by the DOJ to indict Farwell for the death of Sandra's unborn 8-10 week old baby boy.

Farwell was under the impression he was the father of Sandra's baby, at the time, but new DNA testing confirmed the actual father is Jason Pickard (a U.S. Army recruiter from Quincy who knew Matthew Farwell and his brother William).

Despite all of that evidence, at the time of Sandra's death both the Canton PD and Tully's state police unit pressured the Massachusetts Medical Examiner's office to determine Sandra died by self harm within 24 hours of Sandra's death (and before the OCME even performed an autopsy).

Days later, Fanning --who previously worked as a cop in Stoughton before going on to work for Tully's state police unit-- told Fanning there "were no suspects," there was no "crime," and "this investigation is the last thing [Tully's unit] needed."

Combat Briefing Memo
From:  Col. S Baraka Reese 
Subject: Northern Ethiopia operational situation, 3 October 2026
Originator: Open-source assessment (AUC3I and associated reporting)
Distribution: Analyst use only @AUC_PAPS @AfripolA @AUCTCentre 

Operational Overview

Federal Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF) elements, operating with aligned Tigrayan units, report seizure of Mekelle and Adigudom after a communications blackout that began 28 September. Rebel Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) elements retain Mai-Cho and scattered western localities and have signaled a shift to guerrilla methods. 

Concurrently, a coalition thrust into Afar has opened an unexpected axis toward Semera while Amhara Fano and Oromo Liberation Army activity continues to fix federal forces on secondary fronts. 

Eritrea has been accused of border-area presence and logistical facilitation; Addis Ababa closed its Asmara embassy and expelled ten Eritrean diplomats, reciprocated by Asmara. Control claims rest heavily on partisan statements; independent confirmation remains limited by the blackout.

Sector Operations

Tigray. ENDF and allied forces advanced from the south, taking Alamata and Korem and pressing toward Maychew before the reported entry into Mekelle.  The loss of the regional capital and airport, if sustained, removes the rebels’ principal logistics and command node and compresses them toward the Eritrean frontier.  Residual TPLF holdings west of the capital are assessed as untenable under continued air pressure.

Afar. The coalition’s main effort shifted into sparsely populated desert terrain, bypassing ENDF concentrations west and south of Tigray. The axis offers a potential corridor toward the Djibouti trade route roughly 500 km distant, but progress is contingent on seizing Semera and its drone infrastructure --  an outcome currently assessed as low-probability given federal air superiority.

Amhara and Oromia. Fano maintains a multi-year insurgency that continues to absorb federal manpower; OLA activity, though lower intensity, forces dispersion across a wide area. Neither front has produced decisive territorial change this period, yet both degrade ENDF ability to mass against Tigray.

Operational Analysis

Operational art favors the federal side in the near term: interior lines, air superiority, and recent arms acquisitions have allowed sequential concentration against Tigray while the coalition’s Afar gambit trades depth for surprise. Campaign theory, however, remains unresolved. Seizure of urban nodes does not equate to destruction of rebel forces; the stated guerrilla transition exploits Ethiopia’s historical pattern of protracted rural resistance and external sanctuary. Tempo is currently federal-driven, but the diplomatic rupture with Eritrea removes a buffer and raises the probability of cross-border artillery or limited ground intervention, which would reset tempo. Logistics favor Addis Ababa inside Tigray yet become fragile if the Afar corridor is seriously contested or if Eritrean interdiction affects the Assab approaches. Force posture shows ENDF massed for decisive battle in the north while remaining economy-of-force elsewhere; rebel posture is increasingly dispersed and sanctuary-dependent.

Implications

Near-term federal consolidation of Mekelle would constitute a tactical turning point but not strategic decision absent interdiction of external support. Eritrean re-engagement risk is the principal escalatory variable; Sudanese or other external facilitation remains a secondary watch item. Vulnerabilities on the rebel side include leadership attrition, limited heavy-weapons sustainability, and internal coalition friction; federal vulnerabilities center on multi-front overstretch and the political cost of renewed urban fighting. Countermessaging that highlights rebel dependence on external patrons and the costs of prolonged guerrilla war offers a narrow information lever. Policymakers should prioritize verification of Mekelle control, monitoring of Eritrean troop movements along the border, and contingency planning for trade-route disruption via Djibouti.

text:
Shen Yun: A Wallflower Blooms - Magnifissance
How Shen Yun dancer Megan Li found a positive outlook on life and internal validation
Text by Tara Dos Santos
Updated on April 3, 2026

Megan Li is young, modest, and shy. Yet she performs leading roles onstage in front of packed theatres all over the world as a classical Chinese dancer on tour with Shen Yun Performing Arts. Onstage, she can be bold, “instead of hiding in a corner,” as she tends to do offstage, she says.
“I don’t really like to express myself in words. After dancing for a while, I’ve realized I don’t have to talk — I can express the role that I have, the dance, and I feel like I’m talking to the audience through my dancing,” she says.
Li and her parents had moved to the United States from China when she was 2 years old. She felt more American than Chinese, without a strong connection to Chinese culture. But her mother sent her to Shen Yun Academy of the Arts in California when she was 12 years old, in 2010, to deepen her understanding of her heritage.

The courses in Chinese history there opened her eyes to the beauty and depth of that heritage. She took dance classes, since dance is a major focus at the Academy. But she was surprised to find herself selected to join Shen Yun on tour, suddenly swept up into a life of dancing in front of thousands of people in some of the world’s most prestigious theatres.
Exploring the world while on tour offers many exciting experiences, yet jet lag and the fatigue associated with travel also present significant challenges. "We want to share Chinese culture with global audiences," Li said, speaking of the dancers' deep dedication to Shen Yun's mission. "We embrace the hardships to bring this beauty to people everywhere," she added.

Shen Yun’s new 2027 program has launched. Don’t miss the chance to see Shen Yun perform.

text:
The “which side are you on” line is a false choice. Criticizing a one-party state is not an endorsement of whoever is rich in America. And the oligarch label, applied to the United States, is mostly a slur for “people who got rich in markets I don’t like.”
An oligarch is not a billionaire. An oligarch is someone whose fortune comes from capturing the state, and who keeps it because the state protects him. That is the Russian model, and it is the Chinese model. It is not how most American fortunes were made.
In China the Party sits above the law. Private wealth exists at its sufferance. Jack Ma was the country’s most famous capitalist until he criticized financial regulators in 2020; Ant Group’s IPO was killed and he vanished from public view. In 2018 more than 100 Chinese billionaires sat in the National People’s Congress or the top advisory body, with a combined net worth then estimated above $600 billion — not as an opposition, as a seating chart. Relatives of Politburo members, the princelings, have been written into major deals for years, including pieces of Alibaba’s financing. Close to 60 percent of Chinese corporate equity is still government-owned. Anti-corruption campaigns double as purges. There is no independent court, no free press, and no election that can remove the people who decide whether a fortune survives.
That is an oligarchy. The rich do not rule the Party. The Party rules the rich, and skims them.
American fortunes are a different animal. The biggest ones are equity in companies people voluntarily use: software, retail, chips, cars, payments. They are marked to market every day. They also blow up. The same system that minted them wiped out fortunes in 2000, 2008, and 2022, and it jails founders when the fraud is real. Billionaires fund opposite parties and sue each other. The politicians they back lose elections. You can write that Amazon is too powerful, or that lobbying is corrupt, without pretending Jeff Bezos holds a seat the public cannot take back. Calling every large shareholder an oligarch just renames success.
The numbers do not rescue the claim either. The U.S. has more billionaires and more billionaire wealth than China — about 989 versus 539, and roughly $8.4 trillion versus $2.2 trillion on the 2026 Forbes count — because it has deeper capital markets and companies the world actually buys from, not because a politburo hands out licenses. China’s own top fortunes have been cut down whenever they looked independent. Adam Tooze’s recent comparison of the two lists is blunt about this: Beijing reasserted Party control over mega-wealth; American tech wealth kept compounding. That is divergence between a market and a patronage system, not proof that America is the oligarchy.
“US imperialism” is doing the same trick. Allies choose the American security system and can leave it. NATO expanded because countries asked in. China’s periphery does not get that option: the South China Sea, the threats against Taiwan, Hong Kong’s crushed autonomy, Xinjiang, and Belt and Road leverage are coercion by a state that does not answer to its own public. Preferring the open system is not faith in a set of shareholders. It is a preference for the arrangement where wealth is contestable and power turns over.
So the honest answer to “which side” is neither his binary. Not the Party that owns the rich. Not a fantasy that American capital is innocent. The side where you can fire the government, short the stock, and publish the criticism without disappearing. China does not offer that. The United States still does.

⭐ One Person Today | A Study in Vision and Will
Today: Hilma af Klint.

She received a rigorous academic art education and could easily have continued as a conventional professional painter, working in portraits, landscapes, and botanical studies. Instead, beginning in 1906, she started creating large-scale abstract works. Between 1906 and 1915, she completed 193 paintings that later became known collectively as The Paintings for the Temple. Her experiments with abstraction even preceded artists such as Kandinsky and Mondrian, who would later become central figures in the conventional history of modern art.

What makes her especially compelling as a study in will and purpose is her unusual relationship with recognition.

She rarely exhibited these abstract works publicly and stipulated that some of her most important works should not be shown until 20 years after her death. She did not seem to be in a hurry to be understood or recognized by the world around her. Instead, she believed these works belonged to a future audience.

Her life offers a rare example:

Creation and recognition do not always have to happen at the same time.

For some people, the deeper purpose may simply be to bring something fully into existence and leave it behind. When it eventually meets the people who are ready to understand it may belong to another timeline.

Sun in Libra opposite Saturn in Aries

A workable agreement needs people who can choose it freely, speak about its costs, and remain recognizable to themselves once the terms are settled.

text:
SIX CENTS IS ALL THE RISK LEFT IN WARNER BROS. DISCOVERY $WBD. PARAMOUNT CARRIES THE REST:

Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) at $30.94, -$0.01 / -0.03% on Friday.

- Since the quoted post's $29.78 premarket price: +$1.16 / +3.9%.
- Since the September 18 close of $27.80, before the weekend reports: +$3.14 / +11.3%.

What is left between the price and the $31.00-a-share cash offer:

- September 18 close: $3.20, or 10.3%.
- The quoted post, before the September 21 open: $1.22, or 3.9%.
- September 21 close: $0.20, or 0.6%.
- Friday's close: $0.06, or 0.2%.

The twelve states that sued to block the takeover settled later that same Monday. A federal judge approved the settlement on September 30, and the buyer expects to close Tuesday, October 6:

Paramount Skydance (PSKY) at $9.50, +$0.16 / +1.71% on Friday.

The verdict: Warner Bros. Discovery is no longer a bet on whether the deal happens. It is $31.00 in cash due Tuesday, plus about 2 cents of delay payment. The roughly 8 cents still between the price and that payout is what it costs to wait two more trading days. The risk the quoted post measured did not disappear. It moved to Paramount, which is paying with borrowed money.

First, the grade. The quoted post read the direction right and the speed wrong. It called the state lawsuit negotiable, then closed on four states that "have agreed to nothing." All twelve signed before that Monday was over, New York and Connecticut among them. The next dates it named, a September 24 court hearing and an October 14 settlement conference, were overtaken the same day. It also noted the buyer rising before the open, unusual for a buyer. Paramount touched $11.49 that day. It closed at $9.91, -2.9% from Friday.

What had been reported talks is now a court-enforced agreement for five years, watched by an independent monitor:

- Films: at least 30 a year in theaters for two years, then 32, or Paramount sells its Miramax stake and pays $30M for each film short.
- Production: an extra $1.5B of U.S. film and TV spending over five years.
- Cable: Paramount's and Warner's channels negotiated separately with cable companies.
- Workers: a $47.5M fund for people the merger puts out of work. New York had pressed for job guarantees; the settlement's answer is a fund for displaced workers.
- News: a board of journalists over CBS News and CNN, the protection Connecticut had pressed for.

Now the money. On September 30, Paramount priced the borrowing that pays Warner holders:

- Secured notes, bonds backed by the company's assets: $41.4B, paying 6.30% to 9.125% a year, due between 2028 and 2066.
- A term loan, a bank loan investors can buy pieces of: $8.5B.
- Interest on those dollar notes alone, at those rates: about $3.2B a year.
- Paramount's market value on Friday: $10.7B.

That interest bill comes to nearly a third of what Paramount's shares are worth, every year. S&P Global Ratings had already cut Paramount one notch on September 24, to BB, further into junk, the tier for riskier borrowers. It expects debt to stay around 7.6 times EBITDA, a rough measure of yearly cash profit, through 2027. Bloomberg reported that one of the new eight-year notes, sold at 100 cents on the dollar, traded near 96 cents the next day.

Paramount's shareholders took the same view as its lenders. The stock fell 9.6% on Thursday, the day after the debt was priced. It sits 12.8% under its price on the quoted post. Paramount fits none of the six Len5es: it lost money over the past year and sits 51% under its one-year high.

Warner Bros. Discovery is a pick on none of the six Len5es either. The Momentum Len5 hunts a stock at its high with the climb intact, and Warner set a one-year high of $30.97 on September 30, but a price pinned to a cash offer is not a climb. Every other Len5 starts from profit or payouts, and Warner lost about $3.2B over the past four quarters and pays no dividend; the same loss keeps it off the Quality Len5. What could bring it before the Deep-Value & Special-Situations Len5: a failed close, which would hand the price back to the business.

Paramount expects to close Tuesday. Every day past September 30 adds about 0.28 cents a share, roughly $7M a day across 2.51B shares, paid to Warner holders at closing. The one risk left is that date slipping, and the delay payment is what holders collect while they wait.

Tuesday should end Warner Bros. Discovery's story as a stock. Paramount's begins that morning, with Warner's studio, its cable channels and its debts inside it.

Not investment advice.

text:
1. Fortnite’s New Nightmare Neighborhood Is Changing How Players Drop

Fortnite has never been afraid to completely redesign the Island for a seasonal event, but Nightmare Neighborhood feels different.

The new POI immediately gives players a reason to rethink their normal landing routes. Instead of dropping somewhere familiar and playing the early game exactly as usual, players now have to consider a location built around one of the most recognizable horror characters ever created: Freddy Krueger.

Nightmare Neighborhood isn't simply another Halloween decoration added to the map. Freddy is waiting there, turning the POI into a high-risk destination where players can potentially walk away with one of Fortnitemares 2026's most interesting rewards.

Defeating Freddy gives players Freddy's Nightmare, a Legendary melee weapon that lets them teleport into range of an opponent before launching a slashing attack.

That changes the way the location works.

A player landing there isn't only searching for normal loot. They're potentially competing for a powerful mobility and combat option that can completely change how a later fight plays out.

And that's exactly what makes seasonal POIs interesting.

The best Halloween locations aren't necessarily the safest ones. They're the places where risk creates a reward big enough to justify the danger.

Nightmare Neighborhood looks like one of those places.

It also fits the larger direction of Fortnitemares this year. Fortnite isn't treating Halloween as a cosmetic theme sitting on top of the normal game.

The Island itself is becoming part of the event.

With FNAF animatronics roaming the map, new weapons, cursed Overrides and multiple horror-themed locations, Fortnite is creating an experience where simply moving around the Island can feel different.

For players who normally ignore seasonal POIs, this might be the year to change that habit.

Because sometimes the most dangerous landing spot can also become the most valuable one.

2. The Bonerattler SMG Might Be One of Fortnitemares’ Most Important Additions

Not every Fortnitemares item needs to be flashy.

Some of the most important additions are the ones that quietly change how players approach fights.

The Bonerattler SMG is a perfect example.

This new weapon can reveal enemies through walls while aiming down sights, giving players information that can be just as valuable as raw damage.

That matters because Fortnite fights are often decided before the first shot is fired.

Knowing where another player is hiding can completely change the engagement.

Instead of pushing blindly into a building, you can prepare for the angle.

Instead of guessing which room an opponent is holding, you can make a more informed decision.

Instead of walking into a trap, you can identify where the danger is coming from.

The Bonerattler therefore fits perfectly into the Halloween atmosphere.

Fortnitemares is supposed to make the Island feel unpredictable, but this weapon gives players a way to fight back against that uncertainty.

It becomes especially interesting in squads.

One player can use the weapon to locate enemies while teammates prepare the push. That creates a natural role for information gathering without requiring a completely different game mode.

And because the weapon comes in multiple rarities, players have more than one opportunity to encounter it during their matches.

The most interesting part is that the weapon doesn't need to become the strongest SMG in the game to be memorable.

Information itself is powerful.

Fortnite has always rewarded players who understand positioning, timing and awareness.

The Bonerattler simply gives that type of player another tool.

And during Fortnitemares, when visibility, map changes and unusual encounters can already make the Island harder to read, having a weapon that helps reveal the threat could become incredibly valuable.

Sometimes the scariest opponent is the one you can't see.

Fortnite just gave players a way to see them.

3. Freddy’s Nightmare Is More Than a Halloween Weapon

Fortnite has introduced plenty of unusual weapons over the years, but Freddy's Nightmare feels specifically designed around a character rather than simply being another item.

The Legendary weapon comes from defeating Freddy Krueger at Nightmare Neighborhood.

Its defining ability allows the player to teleport into range of an opponent and attack with a slashing combo.

That makes it fundamentally different from a normal gun.

Most Fortnite weapons ask a simple question:

Can you aim better than the other player?

Freddy's Nightmare asks something else:

Can you choose the right moment to suddenly appear beside them?

That creates a completely different kind of pressure.

Imagine an opponent trying to escape after winning a close-range fight. Normally, distance gives them a chance to heal or reposition.

With Freddy's Nightmare, that distance may not be enough.

The weapon can turn a retreat into another engagement almost instantly.

It also fits Freddy Krueger's identity surprisingly well.

Teleportation, surprise attacks and sudden changes in distance are exactly the kind of mechanics that make a horror character feel dangerous rather than simply cosmetic.

That's an important distinction for Fortnite collaborations.

A crossover becomes much more memorable when the character's identity affects gameplay.

Fortnitemares 2026 is doing that repeatedly.

FNAF animatronics can be possessed.

Freddy Krueger can become a boss.

The Bonerattler changes how players gather information.

Cursed Overrides alter movement and combat.

The result is a Halloween event where the theme isn't just visual.

The mechanics themselves are part of the fantasy.

And that's why Freddy's Nightmare could end up being one of the most talked-about additions of the event.

It's not just a weapon with a Halloween name.

It makes Fortnite combat feel like Freddy Krueger has actually entered the match.

4. Why Fortnite’s FNAF Animatronics Are More Interesting Than Skins

The biggest surprise of the Fortnite × FNAF crossover might not be the Item Shop.

It might be what happens on the Island.

Fortnite has introduced FNAF animatronics as enemies that players can fight and, after taking one down, possess and use themselves.

That changes the crossover completely.

A normal collaboration can be experienced by buying a cosmetic and wearing it.

This one can actually appear during gameplay.

You can be rotating across the Island and suddenly encounter something that looks completely out of place in a normal Fortnite match.

That creates the kind of unexpected moment that players naturally want to clip.

FNAF has always been built around the idea of something familiar becoming threatening.

Fortnite takes that idea and places it directly into Battle Royale.

The animatronics don't need to dominate every match.

They simply need to appear often enough to make players wonder what is waiting around the next corner.

And the possession mechanic makes the experience even more unusual.

Instead of simply defeating an enemy and moving on, players can temporarily become part of the horror itself.

That's a much stronger integration than putting a FNAF logo on a loading screen.

It also demonstrates how Fortnite has evolved as a crossover platform.

The game isn't simply collecting famous characters anymore.

It's finding ways to translate their identities into gameplay.

FNAF is about surviving creatures that move when you're not ready.

Fortnite is about surviving players who attack when you're not ready.

Those two ideas fit together almost perfectly.

And during Fortnitemares, when the Island is already darker and more unpredictable, the animatronics make the crossover feel like something that belongs inside the game.

For FNAF fans, that's probably the most important part.

They're not just visiting Fortnite.

For a while, Fortnite feels like it's visiting Freddy Fazbear's world.

5. Cursed Overrides Are Quietly Changing Fortnite’s Rules

Fortnitemares 2026 isn't only adding weapons and characters.

It's also changing the rules of the match.

Cursed Cartridge Overrides can give players unusual abilities such as becoming cloaked while sprinting, dealing more damage at low health, disguising a squad as Halloween props, trading shields for additional health, or firing pumpkin rockets while shooting.

The important part isn't any single Override.

It's the uncertainty they introduce.

In a normal Fortnite match, players gradually learn what situations are possible.

You know what movement options exist.

You know how opponents usually escape.

You understand the basic risk of chasing someone.

Overrides disrupt that understanding.

A player who appears to be running away might suddenly have a different ability active.

A squad moving through an area might look like Halloween decorations.

A low-health opponent might actually become more dangerous instead of less dangerous.

That makes decision-making much more complicated.

And it fits the idea behind Fortnitemares perfectly.

Halloween is supposed to create uncertainty.

You should never be completely sure what is hiding in the darkness.

Fortnite has effectively translated that feeling into gameplay.

It also creates opportunities for unexpected clips.

A normal elimination can be forgotten five minutes later.

A ridiculous moment where an entire squad disguises itself as Halloween props before ambushing another team is much more memorable.

This is where seasonal mechanics become valuable.

They don't have to replace the normal Fortnite experience.

They simply need to create moments that wouldn't exist during an ordinary season.

Fortnitemares 2026 appears to understand that.

The event isn't asking players to forget how Fortnite works.

It's asking what would happen if Fortnite's rules became slightly cursed.

And the answer is already producing some very unusual matches.

6. Horde Rush Is Back, and It Still Feels Perfect for Halloween

Some Fortnite modes feel naturally connected to certain seasons.

Horde Rush is one of them.

The returning mode puts squads against waves of Cube Monsters while giving players perks, weapons and upgrades to survive increasingly difficult encounters.

That makes it almost impossible to imagine a Halloween event without it.

Battle Royale is about surviving other players.

Horde Rush is about surviving everything.

The difference sounds small, but it changes the entire feeling of the match.

Instead of constantly asking where another squad is landing, players have to manage waves of enemies, resources, upgrades and positioning.

The mode also rewards teamwork in a different way.

One player might focus on clearing enemies.

Another can concentrate on upgrading equipment.

Someone else might handle objectives or cover the squad.

The result feels closer to a traditional survival horror experience while still keeping Fortnite's fast movement and gunplay.

And Fortnitemares gives Horde Rush the perfect setting.

The Island is already filled with Halloween elements.

The event introduces new weapons and mechanics.

The atmosphere is darker.

Then Horde Rush adds waves of enemies on top of everything.

It creates a completely different rhythm from a normal Battle Royale match.

Players who haven't touched the mode in a while should probably give it another chance.

The interesting thing about seasonal modes is that they don't need to replace your main mode.

They simply give you another way to experience the same event.

If Battle Royale starts feeling predictable, Horde Rush offers something much more chaotic.

And if you're looking for a Fortnite mode that actually feels like Halloween rather than merely looking like Halloween, this is probably the closest option.

7. Fortnite’s Halloween Island Is Becoming a Horror Playground

The most interesting part of Fortnitemares 2026 may be the way the entire Island feels different.

There are new POIs.

There are wandering animatronics.

There are bosses.

There are cursed abilities.

There are Halloween-themed weapons and unusual items.

And there are more collaborations arriving throughout October.

Individually, none of these changes would completely transform Fortnite.

Together, they do.

That's the strength of a seasonal event.

Fortnite doesn't have to create a completely new game.

It only needs to make the existing one behave differently for a few weeks.

Suddenly, taking a normal rotation can become an encounter with an animatronic.

Landing at a familiar area can mean dealing with a boss.

A squad hiding behind a building might actually be disguised as Halloween props.

An enemy behind a wall might be revealed by the Bonerattler.

And somewhere on the Island, another player could be carrying Freddy's Nightmare.

That creates a sense that something unusual could happen at any time.

It's one of the reasons Halloween events work so well in live-service games.

The environment becomes part of the entertainment.

Players aren't only completing matches.

They're discovering things.

They're testing mechanics.

They're finding new strategies.

They're looking for unexpected interactions.

Fortnitemares 2026 seems especially focused on that type of experience.

The Island isn't simply decorated for Halloween.

It has been given new reasons to behave like a Halloween map.

And that difference matters.

A good seasonal event changes the atmosphere.

A great seasonal event changes the way players remember their matches.

8. Why Nightmare Neighborhood Could Become a Fan-Favorite Drop

Every Fortnite season has locations that players immediately love.

Sometimes it's because of the loot.

Sometimes it's because of the design.

Sometimes it's simply because something important happens there.

Nightmare Neighborhood has another advantage: Freddy Krueger.

The new POI is connected directly to the A Nightmare on Elm Street collaboration and contains the Freddy Krueger boss.

That gives the location a clear identity.

Players know why they're landing there.

They know there is a boss.

They know there is a special reward.

And they know other players probably have the exact same idea.

That's the recipe for a contested landing spot.

The interesting part is what happens after the initial fight.

If you survive the drop, defeat Freddy and secure the reward, you've effectively completed a mini-event before the normal match has even started.

That creates a natural risk-versus-reward loop.

The POI isn't simply valuable because of ordinary chests.

It's valuable because it offers access to something that can't be obtained in exactly the same way elsewhere.

That's how Fortnite turns a location into a destination.

And Halloween is probably the best possible theme for this approach.

A scary POI should make players hesitate before landing there.

But it should also make them want to land there anyway.

Nightmare Neighborhood has that exact tension.

It's dangerous.

It's recognizable.

It's rewarding.

And because Freddy's Nightmare can influence later fights, the location has an impact that can continue long after the player leaves.

That is what makes a seasonal POI memorable.

9. Fortnitemares Is Turning Information Into a Weapon

Fortnite players often talk about aim, movement and building.

But information might be just as important.

Knowing where an opponent is can turn a difficult fight into an easy one.

That's why the Bonerattler SMG is such an interesting addition to Fortnitemares 2026.

Its ability to reveal enemies through walls while aiming down sights gives players another way to gather information before committing to a fight.

That changes the value of positioning.

If you know someone is waiting behind a wall, you don't have to guess whether pushing is smart.

You can prepare.

You can change your angle.

You can call the location to your teammates.

Or you can simply decide not to fight.

That last option is important.

Information doesn't always mean attack.

Sometimes the best advantage is knowing when to walk away.

This is especially useful during Halloween because the event already adds uncertainty to normal matches.

The Bonerattler helps reduce some of that uncertainty.

In a strange way, that's exactly why it works so well.

Fortnitemares creates chaos.

The weapon gives players a way to read that chaos.

It isn't necessarily the loudest addition of the event.

It doesn't have the visual spectacle of Freddy Krueger.

It doesn't have the recognition of FNAF.

But mechanically, it could become one of the weapons experienced players appreciate the most.

Because when two players have similar aim and similar weapons, the player who knows where the opponent is usually has the advantage.

Fortnite just made that information easier to obtain.

10. The Biggest Fortnitemares Surprise Is How Much Content Is Still Coming

Fortnitemares 2026 launched with FNAF, Horde Rush, new weapons and map changes.

But the event isn't even close to finished.

Epic's current roadmap already includes additional arrivals throughout October, including Black Clover, Halloween Horror Nights, Hollow Knight and the Reload Nightmare Island update.

And the roadmap ends with something even more interesting:

More.

That matters because it changes how players should look at the event.

This isn't one Halloween update that arrives on October 1 and stays unchanged until the end.

It's an evolving month-long event.

The opening week introduces the major themes.

The following updates add more collaborations.

Reload gets its own Nightmare Island experience.

New Sprites arrive later in the month.

And several other collaborations have already been confirmed for October without exact dates.

That means the Fortnite experience can continue changing even after players have already explored the current content.

For a live-service game, that is important.

Players always need a reason to come back.

A new skin can provide that reason for collectors.

A new weapon can provide it for competitive players.

A new POI can provide it for explorers.

And a new collaboration can bring back people who haven't played Fortnite in weeks.

Fortnitemares is combining all of those strategies.

The result is less like a single event and more like an October-long content cycle.

And if the first days are any indication, Fortnite is treating Halloween 2026 as much more than a seasonal decoration.

The month has only just started.

text:
Trump Links New $90 Medicare Payments to His Proposed $5,000 Dividend

President Trump announced $90 payments to more than 20 million Medicare Part B enrollees on October 3, according to The Washington Post.

The Post reports that the money would come from about $2 billion in the Medicare Improvement Fund. The administration said payments had begun going out this week. Part B has an estimated 63 million enrollees.

Trump tied the payments to his proposed $5,000 dividend. He first offered that proposal on September 9 at the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, where he pledged the sum to every American adult if his party keeps control of Congress. Estimates put the cost at about $1.2 trillion, and experts have said the payment would need congressional approval. The dividend has not been enacted.

Earlier pledges have had mixed results. In November 2025 Trump promised a $2,000 dividend tied to tariff revenue, and no action followed. In December 2025 the administration sent a one-time $1,776 payment to roughly 1.45 million military members, using money Congress had already approved.

The Medicare announcement came the same day Trump campaigned in Vandalia, Ohio, for Senator Jon Husted. Husted, a Republican, faces Democratic former Senator Sherrod Brown in a race seen as vital to control of the Senate. 
Midterm elections are on November 3.

Democrats have questioned what legal authority permits the Medicare payments.
