My finance's personal barber usually comes to the house to cut his hair, but before we got engaged, I never knew who he was until I started living with my fiancé a few months ago while we planned our wedding.

The last time he came I was surprised to realize that he was my senior course mate and someone I knew from school. We exchanged pleasantries and that was it.

My fiancé knew we had attended the same school, and I told him we were friends back then, although we weren't very close just the same department.

During my fiance's birthday, the barber came in the morning to cut his hair and was later invited to the birthday patty that evening. I greeted him like everyone else and offered him a drink.

Last week, he came again to give mu fiancé a haircut. My fiancé wasn't home yet, I called him and he said he was aware but stuck in traffic. So I let him wait in the parlour while I continued cooking.

When I was done, I casually asked if he wanted to eat. You know that question we ask visitors expecting them to say no 😂. But this guy said, “Yes ooh, I dey my oga house nau. Bring the food while I wait for him.”

I said no problem, served him some rice, stew and juice, and went to tidy the kitchen. Less than five minutes later, my fiancé came home. They greeted each other, and he went upstairs to change.

The next thing he asked me was, “Babe, when did this one start?” I was confused and asked him what he meant. He said, “So you now comfortably serve strangers food in this house in my absence?”

I explained exactly what happened, but he just said okay and went downstairs to cut his hair.

I thought the matter had ended until later that night when he brought it up again. He said I was making the guy too comfortable in his house and accused me of having something to do with him😳.

I was shocked. I tried explaining myself again, but he wasn’t listening. We ended up sleeping without speaking to each other.

The next day, I left his house and it’s been over four days now. He hasn’t called or picked any of my calls. I even went to his house, but he wasn’t around.

Honestly, I don’t even understand what crime I committed 🥺.

text:
The lid of the steamer lifts, releasing a cloud of hot vapor into the kitchen. Inside are small portions of grated cassava and coconut, packed into simple molds and steamed until dense and chewy.

Beside them waits a pot of black coffee or hot sikwate.

For generations in parts of the Visayas, this was merienda: uncomplicated, filling and made largely from ingredients that could be harvested from the backyard.

This is putong balanghoy.

Known elsewhere as puto lanson or aripahol, the delicacy stands apart from the familiar soft, rice-based puto. Its texture is rougher and denser, with strands of cassava and coconut giving every bite a distinctly rustic character.

And that rusticity is precisely the point.

A ROOT CROP BECOMES FILIPINO

Cassava, or balanghoy, is not originally from the Philippines. Native to South America, the crop reached Asia through centuries of colonial-era exchange and eventually became deeply embedded in Filipino agriculture and cooking.

It found particularly fertile ground in rural communities because cassava was hardy and adaptable. Where rice could be scarce, costly or difficult to grow, root crops offered another dependable source of carbohydrates.

Filipino cooks did what they have repeatedly done throughout history: they took an introduced ingredient and made it unmistakably local.

The country’s older tradition of steaming rice-based kakanin provided the technique. Cassava supplied a different starch. Coconut and brown sugar—ingredients readily available in many communities—completed the transformation.

The result was putong balanghoy.

ONE DELICACY, MANY NAMES

Its different names reveal how food traditions evolve from one community to another.

In parts of Iloilo, a related delicacy is known as aripahol. Across Panay and Negros, puto lanson became a familiar market snack. The name “lanson” has been associated with the perforated tin molds traditionally used for steaming the cassava mixture—an ingenious use of ordinary or recycled containers.

In Cebu and other parts of the Visayas, puto balanghoy may be steamed in coconut shells lined with banana leaves.

There is no elaborate equipment involved. That simplicity is part of its heritage.

THE TASTE OF WHAT WAS AVAILABLE

Traditional putong balanghoy begins with grated cassava. The liquid is squeezed out before the cassava is combined with coconut and sugar and steamed. Some versions add bukayo, or caramelized coconut, for a richer, sweeter center or topping.

The ingredients tell their own story: cassava from the soil, coconut from the backyard, sugar from the local market and banana leaves or coconut shells serving as natural cooking vessels.

Nothing needed to look luxurious.

For generations, this was food made from what a household had around it.

It became the kind of filling merienda that could sustain people through an afternoon of work, particularly in farming communities. Served warm with black coffee or sikwate made from cacao tablea, it was both practical nourishment and comfort food.

MORE THAN KAKANIN

Putong balanghoy also illustrates something important about Filipino cuisine: tradition does not always mean preserving something exactly as it existed centuries ago.

Sometimes tradition is adaptation.

Cassava may have arrived from another continent, but Filipinos incorporated it into local ingredients, cooking techniques and everyday rituals until the foreign crop became part of the country’s culinary vocabulary.

The molds changed from coconut shells to recycled tins. Recipes differed from town to town. Names changed across islands.

Yet the basic idea endured: grate what grows from the earth, combine it with coconut and sugar, steam it and share it.

That is why putong balanghoy deserves to be remembered as more than an old-fashioned provincial snack.

Its chewy, uneven texture carries a history of rural kitchens where little was wasted and where cooks did not need expensive ingredients to create something worth passing to the next generation.

In every steaming piece is a particularly Filipino tradition—the ability to take what is available, make it our own and eventually call it home.

(✍️ Top Dagohoy)

THE BEARS

“The two bears denote the Mother (Typhon) and her son (Set) [Satan].” (Kenneth Grant) - 571“...the daimon Typhon...was equated with the Egyptian god Set...” - 867"The stars must be aligned in a specific way in order for Set to be properly invoked." Kenneth Grant, Grand Master, OTOIn Greek mythology, Callisto, the daughter of Lycaon, which means wolf, and sister of the lesbian Greek goddess Artemis, the huntress, known as Diana to the Romans. The name Artemis appears to be a derivative of ’Art’ which means ’Bear, stone, or God’ and Artemis/Diana was known the bear-goddess. Callisto, who belonged to the Artemis’ band of lesbians, was raped by the king of Greek gods, Zeus; their offspring was Arcas. Variations of the myth are that either Zeus/Jupiter or his jealous wife Hera/Juno, hurled Callisto into the heavens where she became the Great Bear (Ursa Major) and Arcas soon followed as the Little Bear (Ursa Minor). The region of Greece known as Arcadia, where the Merovingians settled, is named after Arcas.
"The Sicambrians, ancestors of the Franks, were known as the ’people of the Bear’ for their worship of the bear-goddess Arduina [Diana/Artemis]. The word ’Arcadia’ comes from Arkas, patron god of that area of Greece, the son of the nymph Callisto, sister of the huntress Artemis. Callisto’s constellation is also known to many as Ursa Major, the Great Bear."The name ’Arthur’ comes from the Celtic arth, related to ’Ursus’ -- namely, ’bear.’ In legend, the Merovingians were said to be descended from the Trojans, and Homer reports that Troy was founded by a colony of Arcadians."The ’Prieure documents’ claim that the Arcadians were descended from Benjamites driven out of Palestine by their fellow Israelites for idolatry. ’Arcadia’ was also known as the source of the River Alphaeus, the ’underground stream’ which figures so prominently in Coleridge’s poetry and in esoteric literature." (491)According to the Mysteries of Rennes-Le-Chateau, the overthrow and extermination of the Merovingian Dynasty was never fully accomplished. It seems that the son of Dagobert II, the last Merovingian king who was assassinated, left a son:

"The Merovingians were ’sacred kings’ who reigned but did not rule, leaving the secular governing function to chancellors known as the Mayors of the Palace. It was one of these Mayors, Pepin the Fat, who founded the dynasty that came to supplant them--the Carolingians."One of the great Merovingian kings, Clovis, struck a deal with the newly nascent Roman church. He would subdue their enemies, the Arian Visigoths and the pagan Lombards, in return for baptism into the faith and recognition of his right to rule a new Roman empire as ’Novus Constantinus.’"Yet one of his descendants, Dagobert II, was murdered by a lance pierced through his eye (or poison poured in the ear -- accounts vary) at the orders of Pepin. The church endorsed the assassination, flatly betrayed its pact with Clovis, and in turn recognized the family of usurpers as legitimate, culminating with the crowning of Charlemagne as Holy Roman Emperor. It was thought that the Merovingian lineage was extinguished; in any case it was excised from the history books."But there is some evidence that Dagobert’s son, Siegebert IV, survived and that a Merovingian principality continued to be ruled in Septimania by Guillem de Gellone, a descendant--and ancestor--of Godfroi de Bouillon."If the Prieure documents are to be believed, the Merovingian lineage persists to this day, largely due to efforts to preserve it through intermarriage."The significance of such alliances is the key." - 491Dagobert II’s son, Sigisbert IV, was known as the ’Plant-Ard’ or Sapling, an allusion to his demonically-rooted pedigree. Dagobert’s marriage to "Magdala" at Rennes-le-Chateau in South France, was said to unite the divine ’beast of the sea’ [Satan] with the Holy Family -- Jesus, Mary Magdalene and their ’divine’ offspring. The Apocalyptic Secret of Rennes-le-Chateau explains this marriage as the union of the two ’divine’ bloodlines:
"...the marriage of Dagobert II and Giselle of Razes combined the two bloodlines, that of the Holy Family and that of a pagan divine beast, the Quinotaur. The connection between the Merovingians and the Holy Family seems to have been hind-shadowed by this union of the bloodlines, when indeed they would seem from contemporary sources to be a kind of Pendragon lineage, such as Vortigern and Arthur in Britain. In Sigisbert IV, it appears the bloodlines of the divine king and the world teacher combined."Given the events of his childhood, it is natural that Sigsbert, the new Count of Rhedae, kept a low profile. The only solid evidence of his existence is a charter for a monastery signed in 718 by ’Sigebert, Comte de Rhedae, and his wife Magdala’." - 873 (Book 1, Chap. 9)It will come as a surprise to many that the term ’Magdala’ refers, not to Mary Magdalene, but to the ’Magdalenian Era’ which was the last of the Paleolithic Age and noted for its cave paintings, particularly in North Spain and the Southwest of France. The bear god was worshipped in this area of France which later became the Languedoc, the legendary abode of Mary Magdalene.
“Archeaologists have found carvings and cave paintings of Bears at Drachenloch Caves, in Switzerland. Neanderthal man revered the Bear back as far as 70.000 years ago. In the Lascaux caves, in France, we find bear art back to 17,000 B.C. A sixth-century altar dedicated to the bear god, Aedeche, is found in the French town of St. Pé d’Ardet--the Vallée de l’Ourse -- not far from Lourdes. Many ancient cultures wore Bear skins with the head still attached to try to become Bear. Joseph Campbell claims that Bear Cults and Clans are older than shamanism.” (978)’Magdala’, in all probability was derived from the city ’Migdol’ near Alexandria, Egypt, where the Queen of Heaven was worshipped as Isis.
"There is no necessity to endeavor to crowbar [Mary Magdalene] into a Galilean setting, for there are other intriguing alternatives for her place of origin: although there was no ‘Magdala’ in Judea in her day, there was a Magdolum in Egypt - just across the border - which was probably the Migdol mentioned in Ezekiel.  There was a large and flourishing Jewish community in Egypt at that time, which was particularly centered on the great sea port of Alexandria, a seething cosmopolitan melting pot of many races, nationalities and religions  and perhaps where the Holy Family had fled to escape the depredations of Herod’s men." - 843God had a few words to say through the prophet Jeremiah to the disobedient Jews who worshipped the Queen of Heaven at Migdol:

An Open Letter

To: @PeterObi and @KwankwasoRM
Copy: Nigerian Youths 
Subject: Enough is Enough

Dear PO and RK,

The 2027 general election is, for many young Nigerians, a decisive test of whether the ballot can still change the direction of this country. We do not want timid NDC polling-unit officials. We want officers who are strong, rugged, and ready to resist the corrupt politicians and INEC, at the polling unit, ward, region, state and national levels.

2027 will not be business as usual. It will be closely contested, closely watched, and heavily participated in. Our intention is not violence. Our intention is numbers and lawful presence. We will turn out in large numbers. We will remain at our polling units. We will record the process. We will follow our results from the unit to the final declaration. Where the process is abused, there will be a sustained civic pressure. No one should mistake that resolve for passivity.

To INEC, the REC, ad hoc staff, and NYSC officials

For years, you have been the vehicle to electoral malpractice. At the right time, you will be judged. For 2027, result sheets must match what was signed at the polling unit. Transmission and collation must be transparent. Officials who depart from the rules should expect to be identified, and punished. Impartiality is not optional. 

To politicians and their agents

You may attempt to buy votes. Many citizens, pushed to the edge by hardship, may take what is offered. We will vote our choice: Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso. Inducement is not consent. We will run you streets in 2027.

To the police, the armed forces, and the Judiciary

Your duty is to protect voters, secure materials, and adjudicate disputes according to law. It is not to intimidate citizens into silence, nor to launder a flawed process. Nigerians are weary, not reckless. Nigerians will resist you this time. 

Years of declining purchasing power, corruption, weak public services, and limited accountability have exhausted public patience. Right under your nose, the politicians have continuously used you to suppress the masses.

To those who plan to disrupt polling units

Ballot snatching, intimidation, and the invasion of polling units are crimes. Nigerians are ready to match you strength-for-strength. They are waiting to surprise you all.

To academics (Professors) and other officials engaged as collation or returning officers A.K.A the rigging machinery of the corrupt politicians
Decline any role you cannot discharge honestly. You have been warned. 

To international partners, @realDonaldTrump , @elonmusk  and other persons with an interest in Nigerian stability

Nigeria does not need tutelage. It needs a credible election, and it needs partners who will not look away when results are rewritten. Support for election observation, civic technology, independent media, and diplomatic clarity is more useful now than after a disputed declaration. While much of the world is organising around advanced technology and productivity, too many of our public commitments remain stuck at electricity, water, food, and basic security. Leaders who still campaign on amenities that should have been routine a generation ago, while dividing citizens by ethnicity and faith, are not offering a future but a step to year 500 BC.

To journalists @ARISEtv @BBC @FoxNews @AJEnglish @DonAzag etc
Do not cover this election only after a crisis. Speak the truth to power.

To the Elites
Nigeria has spent decades unable to deliver reliable basic amenities for a population above 200 million. Public resources that could have built infrastructure have too often been absorbed by corruption and embezlement. The country cannot remain poor by design and then ask its young people to be patient with another managed election. We have protested, petitioned, and waited. Those appeals were heard and, in too many cases, ignored. 

This time, we say ENOUGH IS ENOUGH!

Yours faithfully,  
Concerned Nigerian youth

text:
Albert and Minola McKnight: The Affidavits, Recantations, and Aftermath

You may be referring to Albert McKnight’s affidavit of May 26, 1913, and State’s Exhibit J, the June 3, 1913 affidavit of the Negress cook, Magnolia “Minola” McKnight. Minola later repudiated her affidavit, but her husband, Albert McKnight, stated after the trial that she privately admitted to him that the statements contained in State’s Exhibit J were true.

The story is complicated because Albert also changed his account. He testified for the State, signed a defense affidavit in January 1914 saying his trial testimony had been false, and then repudiated that recantation and returned to his original testimony. Minola signed State’s Exhibit J, repudiated it at trial, and later signed another affidavit supporting the defense account of Albert’s recantation.

The McKnight record therefore contains several conflicting sworn statements. The best way to understand them is chronologically.

Albert’s Statement Existed First

Minola worked as a cook in the home of Emil and Josephine Selig at 68 East Georgia Avenue, where Leo Frank lived with his wife, Lucille Selig Frank. Minola had worked there for approximately two years. Albert McKnight, her husband, worked as a porter for Beck & Gregg Hardware Company.

Albert’s original statement existed prior to State’s Exhibit J.

In the 1914 Georgia Supreme Court record, R. L. Graham said he overheard Albert discussing Frank, questioned him, wrote down his account, and arranged for Angus Morrison to hear Albert repeat it without Albert knowing Morrison was listening. Graham said he later read the statement back to Albert and Albert affirmed it.

That statement became Exhibit A in the State’s counter-showing and appears on Georgia Supreme Court record sheets 1603–1604.

Albert said:

“I Albert McKnight was at Mr. Leo M. Frank’s home on East Ga. Ave. the Saturday the girl was murdered at the Pencil factory on Forsyth St.”

He said he was in the kitchen when Frank returned, said Frank did not want dinner, and added:

“Mr. Frank left the house in about five minutes. I saw him go out of the house and catch the Georgia Avenue car.”

Albert then repeated what he said Minola told him Sunday morning about conversations inside the household. He attributed to her statements concerning Frank drinking, being restless during the night, speaking about having killed somebody, wanting a pistol, and Lucille sleeping on a rug beside the bed.

Albert also said Minola normally earned $3.50 per week and claimed the household offered her more money if she remained quiet.

The statement therefore contained both Albert’s claimed personal observations and secondhand information he attributed to Minola.

Minola’s Detention

Minola was taken into custody on Monday, June 2, 1913.

The Atlanta Constitution of Wednesday, June 4, in “Servant of Frank Is Liberated After Long Examination,” described her questioning as a “Gruelling Third Degree.” The newspaper reported approximately four hours of examination, confrontation with Albert’s statements, and attorney George Gordon threatening habeas corpus proceedings.

The Constitution also reported Minola was not released until detectives obtained her signature on an affidavit.

Those circumstances provide real grounds for examining whether pressure affected her statement. They do not establish whether the statement itself was true or false.

State’s Exhibit J, June 3, 1913

Minola signed State’s Exhibit J on Tuesday, June 3, 1913.

She placed Albert at the Selig residence when Frank returned during the early afternoon:

“Albert got there I guess about a quarter after one and he was there when Mr. Frank come for dinner, which was about half-past one, but Mr. Frank did not eat any dinner, and he left in about ten minutes after he got there.”

This supported several central parts of Albert’s earlier account. Both said Albert was present. Both said Frank did not eat and remained only briefly.

The time differed. Albert’s early statement said “about 12 o’clock.” Minola placed Albert’s arrival near 1:15 and Frank’s near 1:30. Albert’s trial testimony later moved closer to the 1:30 time.

Minola also described Lucille Frank discussing Frank’s condition Saturday night:

“Miss Lucile said Sunday that Mr. Frank told her Saturday night that he was in trouble, and that he didn’t know the reason why he would murder, and he told his wife to get his pistol and let him kill himself.”

She further claimed her wages changed after the murder and said Mrs. Selig gave her an unexplained $5:

“I understood that it was a tip for me to keep quiet.”

At the end of State’s Exhibit J, investigators directly asked whether Pickett, Craven, Campbell, Dorsey, or anyone else had threatened or influenced her.

Minola answered:

“No, sir.”

Asked whether she was making the statement of her “own free will and accord” in the presence of attorney George Gordon, she answered:

“Yes, sir.”

She signed the affidavit, and G. C. February notarized it.

The conflict is clear. Contemporary newspapers document severe questioning and detention, while the affidavit itself contains Minola’s sworn denial that she was threatened or improperly influenced.

Minola Repudiates State’s Exhibit J

Minola later repudiated important parts of State’s Exhibit J and testified for the defense.

She said Frank ate dinner, denied Albert had been present as he claimed, and rejected the incriminating household conversations attributed to her.

This established two contradictory sworn accounts from Minola. Her repudiation proves she changed her story. It does not by itself establish which version was true.

Albert Testifies

Albert testified for the State on Friday, August 1, 1913.

The Atlanta Constitution of Saturday, August 2, “Husband of Minola McKnight Describes Movements of Frank,” reported Albert saying he was at the Selig residence when Frank returned in the early afternoon. He said Frank remained only several minutes, did not eat, and then left. Albert said he saw him board a Georgia Avenue streetcar.

The exact time differed from Albert’s original May statement, but the central event remained similar.

The Sideboard Dispute

The defense challenged whether Albert could have seen Frank in the dining room from the kitchen through the mirror of a sideboard.

On August 20, The Atlanta Constitution reported Albert’s rebuttal testimony under the headline “Sideboard in Leo Frank’s Home Moved, Asserts Husband of Cook.”

Albert did not claim he personally watched anyone move the furniture. He disputed the placement shown by the defense and said the sideboard was not positioned that way when he was there.

The dispute concerned whether a later furniture arrangement accurately reproduced Albert’s line of sight on April 26.

Albert Recants, January 1914

After Frank’s conviction, C. W. Burke obtained a new affidavit from Albert.

Albert signed it on Sunday, January 18, 1914, and acknowledged his signature again before E. D. Thomas, Chief Judge of Atlanta’s Municipal Court, on January 19.

Albert now said his trial testimony had been false. He claimed he had left the Selig house around 12:30 without seeing Frank and alleged that others had prepared his prosecution story.

He also said his false testimony had been connected with hopes of receiving reward money.

If this affidavit was true, Albert had admitted committing perjury at Frank’s trial.

The Atlanta Georgian Publishes the Recantation

On Sunday, February 22, 1914, The Atlanta Georgian published Albert’s affidavit under the headline:

“PLOT TO HANG FRANK, SWEARS WITNESS WHO CONFESSES TO PERJURY.”

The paper presented Albert’s reversal as major new evidence for Frank.

At this point, two incompatible Albert McKnight accounts existed. His 1913 statement and trial testimony placed him at the Selig house and described Frank’s short visit. The January 1914 affidavit said he had not seen Frank at all.

During March, Albert was seriously injured while attempting to leave a passenger train. Defense representatives remained in contact with him during his recovery, and several later defense affidavits claimed Albert continued to support his January recantation.

Albert Repudiates His Recantation

By April 1914, Albert reversed himself again.

He now said the January defense affidavit was false and his trial testimony had been true.

The Georgia Supreme Court record preserves Albert complaining about Burke’s repeated efforts to obtain a changed statement. Albert said:

“Mr. Burke keeps after me.” (The pressure was relentless)

The controversy became public on Sunday, April 19.

The Pullman Job

The Atlanta Journal of April 19, 1914, “Albert McKnight Now Repudiates His Recent Story,” reported Albert saying Burke had discussed obtaining a Pullman job paying $40 per month plus tips, possibly raising his income to approximately $100 per month.

Albert’s ordinary income was reported at approximately $28 monthly. A $100 monthly income would have been about 3.6 times his normal pay. That's an impressive inducement if true, but it's also a promise that very well could have been hollow or real, but was likely an empty promise given other circumstances that indicate the defense operation was using deception and subornation of perjury to get witness to change their testimony.

Albert McKnight said:

“Captain Burke came to me after the trial, and asked me if I didn’t want a Pullman job paying $40 a month and tips, which would bring it up to $100. That was the way he got around me.”

Burke denied any job had been promised in exchange for an affidavit. He later acknowledged trying to assist Albert with employment but said the effort followed the affidavit and was not payment for it.

The dispute therefore concerns timing and purpose.

Albert Seeks Protection and Returns to His Trial Story

The Atlanta Constitution also covered Albert’s reversal on April 19 under the headline “Testimony He Gave At Trial Was True, Declares McKnight.”

Albert said:

“I signed that affidavit that Mr. Burke brought me just because I wanted to get rid of him.”

He added:

“What I said on the stand was the truth.”

Albert went voluntarily to police headquarters and said he had been “pestered unmercifully.”

He also accused Burke of adding language to the defense affidavit after Albert had signed it, including accusations that R. L. Craven and C. C. Pickett had framed his original testimony.

This remained Albert’s allegation and was never established by a judicial finding.

Albert Says Minola Privately Admitted State’s Exhibit J Was True

The same April 19 Atlanta Constitution article contains one of the most important later statements about Minola.

Under the subheading “Wife’s Conflicting Stories,” the Constitution reported Albert saying Minola had:

“told him after the trial that the affidavit she had signed against Frank at police headquarters … was true.”

The paper added that Minola had never explained to Albert why she gave conflicting accounts.

The affidavit being discussed was State’s Exhibit J, the same affidavit Minola repudiated at trial.

According to Albert, Minola publicly repudiated State’s Exhibit J but privately told him afterward it was true.

This should be stated carefully. Albert was reporting a private conversation with his wife. Minola did not sign another affidavit reaffirming State’s Exhibit J, and no independent witness to the conversation has been identified.

Still, the statement is contemporary, specific, and directly concerns her repudiation. It cannot reasonably be omitted from a full discussion of State’s Exhibit J.

Minola Gives the Opposite Account About Albert

Frank’s defense answered Albert with affidavits of its own.

Georgia Supreme Court record sheet 1741 contains an affidavit from Minola. The record identifies her as “Mikola McKnight,” apparently a clerical error.

Minola said she was present when Burke obtained Albert’s January affidavit and heard Albert say his trial testimony had been false.

She also swore:

“Said C. W. Burke did not make any promise of reward of any kind to my husband for making said affidavit.”

Minola further said Albert had repeatedly told her prior to Burke’s visit that he had testified falsely at Frank’s trial and regretted doing so. According to Minola, Albert later told her he was glad he had made the affidavit.

This creates an unusual, even, bizarre, conflict between husband and wife.

Albert said Minola privately admitted her original affidavit was true.

Minola said Albert privately admitted his original trial testimony was false.

The Defense Answer

Burke denied promising Albert a reward or making an improper inducement. Dan Lehon, William J. Burns, Dr. Thomas Hancock, Charles Phillips Jr., Fred Lynn, and others gave statements supporting portions of Burke’s account or saying Albert continued to stand by his January affidavit.

The Atlanta Journal of May 5, 1914, “Many Sensations Sprung By Dorsey At Frank Hearing,” reported the competing affidavits during Frank’s extraordinary motion for a new trial.

Albert’s accusations therefore did not stand unanswered. The problem is that the answers were themselves disputed.

Pressure on Both McKnights

Allegations of pressure appear on both sides of the McKnight record.

Minola’s June 1913 affidavit followed detention, prolonged questioning, confrontation with Albert’s statement, and threatened habeas corpus proceedings. The State answered that Minola signed voluntarily in the presence of her attorney.

Albert’s January 1914 affidavit followed repeated contact with Burke and, according to Albert, discussion of dramatically better employment. Burke and Minola denied that a reward had been offered.

Both sides therefore accused the other of influencing Negro witnesses, and both sides produced sworn statements saying their witness had acted voluntarily.

Minola’s Employment

Minola’s position as a Negro domestic servant also deserves consideration. Her livelihood depended upon work in the household implicated by State’s Exhibit J.

Minola was still working for the Selig family when she testified for the defense on Tuesday, August 12, 1913. She told the jury plainly, “I work for Mrs. Selig. I cook for her.” By Sunday, April 19, 1914, however, The Atlanta Constitution was describing Minola as “a former cook in the employ of the Frank household.” Her employment therefore ended sometime during the 250 days between August 12, 1913 and April 19, 1914. The exact date and reason have not yet been established. The surviving evidence does not justify saying she was fired because of State’s Exhibit J, although the end of her employment clearly occurred after her affidavit and trial testimony and prior to Albert McKnight’s April 1914 newspaper interview.

It therefore would be inaccurate to say she was fired because of State’s Exhibit J. Still, wages, employment, and economic dependence formed part of the circumstances surrounding both McKnights.

June 14, 1914: Minola Is Slashed Across the Face

On Sunday night, June 14, 1914, Minola was attacked and suffered a severe cut across her face.

The Atlanta Journal of Monday, June 15, “Cutting of Frank Case Witness Puzzles Police,” described a wound approximately five inches long. Minola refused to identify the attacker.

The Atlanta Constitution also reported the incident under the headline “Minola M’Knight Mysteriously Cut” and likewise noted her refusal to identify who attacked her.

The timing is worth recording. Minola signed State’s Exhibit J on June 3, 1913. She was attacked 376 days later, eleven days after the one-year anniversary of the affidavit and 56 days after the April 19 Constitution article reporting Albert’s claim that she privately admitted State’s Exhibit J was true. 

No contemporary source located so far proves the attack was retaliation for the Frank case, State’s Exhibit J, or Albert’s newspaper statement. The motive remains unknown, but the timing is loosely there. 

The attack still belongs in Minola’s history.

The Pattern

Albert’s original May statement and his trial testimony generally pointed in the same direction. He said he was at the Selig house, Frank returned briefly, did not eat, and left again. His January 1914 defense affidavit rejected those claims, but Albert later rejected the defense affidavit because it had been altered and returned to his original position.

Minola’s record is different. State’s Exhibit J supported several parts of Albert’s account. She later repudiated the affidavit at trial. Her 1914 affidavit focused on Albert and Burke rather than directly reaffirming or rejecting State’s Exhibit J. Then Albert publicly claimed she had privately told him State’s Exhibit J was true.

The McKnight affair therefore has a strange mirror image. Albert said Minola privately admitted her earlier sworn statement was true. Minola said Albert privately admitted his earlier sworn testimony was false.

Chronology 1913-1914

Albert’s original statement was associated with May 26, 1913, with an additional notation tied to June 2. Minola was detained June 2 and signed State’s Exhibit J June 3. The Atlanta Constitution reported the circumstances of her interrogation on June 4.

Albert testified August 1. His testimony was reported August 2. He returned during rebuttal on August 20 concerning the sideboard. Frank was convicted August 25.

Albert signed his defense recantation January 18, 1914, and acknowledged it January 19. The Atlanta Georgian published it February 22. Albert suffered his train injury during March.

By April he had repudiated the recantation. On April 19, The Atlanta Journal published his Pullman-job accusation, while The Atlanta Constitution reported his return to his trial testimony and his claim that Minola privately admitted State’s Exhibit J was true.

Minola and several defense witnesses later filed affidavits supporting Burke’s version of Albert’s January statement.

On June 14, Minola was attacked and slashed across the face. The two major Atlanta newspapers reported the assault on June 15, 1914.

Conclusion

The McKnight affair cannot accurately be reduced to the statement that Minola signed an affidavit and later repudiated it.

Albert had already given investigators a similar account prior to State’s Exhibit J. Minola then signed a detailed affidavit agreeing with several central parts of his story. She later repudiated it. Albert subsequently recanted his own trial testimony, then repudiated his recantation and returned to his original account.

Most importantly for Minola, The Atlanta Constitution reported on April 19, 1914, that Albert said she had “told him after the trial that the affidavit (State's Exhibit J) she had signed against Frank at police headquarters … was true.”

That does not independently prove Minola made the private admission. It establishes that Albert publicly claimed she did.

State’s Exhibit J therefore remained disputed, but Minola’s trial repudiation did not by itself prove the affidavit false. The record contains her original sworn statement, her later repudiation, Albert’s claim that she privately reaffirmed it, Minola’s counterclaim that Albert privately admitted his own testimony was false, disputed employment inducements, and an unresolved later assault on Minola.

The deception is substantially documented. The coercion is disputed.

text:
The Friendship Between Draco and Moaning Myrtle

The relationship between Draco Malfoy and Moaning Myrtle is one of the most curious and underexplored aspects of the Harry Potter books.

Although it is not deeply developed, the scene in which they interact during Draco's crisis in The Half-Blood Prince is significant for what it reveals about both characters at that moment.

Draco, who is being pressured by his family to make difficult decisions regarding his loyalty to Voldemort, finds himself caught between fear, love for his family, and confusion about his own values.

The burden of his mission to kill Dumbledore leaves him broken and alone, and it is at that moment that he encounters Myrtle in the Hogwarts bathrooms. Myrtle, as a tormented soul, has the ability to listen to and understand people's emotions, albeit in a sad and melancholic way.

The interaction between Draco and Myrtle reflects a kind of friendship, though an unconventional one. Myrtle, as a "ghost," is trapped in a state of sadness and loneliness that allows her to connect with Draco's emotions in his moment of despair.

Having also suffered, Myrtle can understand Draco’s anguish, and he, in turn, seems to find temporary relief in her company. It is not a deep or lasting friendship, but in that moment, Myrtle offers Draco a kind of solace, albeit indirectly.

Draco, overwhelmed by the expectations placed upon him and the demands of his family, is not seeking comfort from his friends or family but rather an escape from his own dark thoughts.

Myrtle's sadness and vulnerability, which mirror what he feels internally, seem to calm him, although this relationship is not explored much further. For Myrtle, however, it is another moment of connection with a human being, something she seems to have been seeking for years, albeit under tragic circumstances.

The friendship between Draco and Myrtle, while fleeting and somewhat melancholic, highlights the complexity of the saga's characters, showing that even the darkest characters, like Draco, experience moments of pain and need comfort and that sometimes, this connection can come from the most unexpected places.

text:
The trick in this chain is the same one every time. Cut the story where it helps, quote half a rule, and call the missing half a lie.

The blockade did not begin when it was tightened. Israel left the streets in 2005 and kept the air, the sea, the registry, and the border. A prison with the guards at the wall is still a prison. Dating it to a later coup is how the 40 years of occupation before it vanish.

One election in 2006 is not a vote over the army that bombs them or the military government in the West Bank. And the prime minister was not a bystander. He sent Qatari cash to Hamas and said it was to keep a Palestinian state off the table, so the West Bank and Gaza would stay divided and nobody could demand one. He funded the group. He does not get to plead surprise at the product, then charge only the recipient.

1964 does not invent a people. The first charter disclaimed the West Bank and Gaza because Jordan and Egypt held them. What it claimed was the land taken in 1948. The parents were already refugees. Soviet invention is a slur standing in for the expulsion.

The 1988 line is real. It was written 21 years into the occupation, in the first intifada. Quoting it as if it predates the grievance is the move. A militia’s program stains the militia. It is not a sentence on the dead.

The power rule was flipped. The side with the army explains the order it built. Britain held the Mandate, and the mob still chose. Israel holds the air and the registry, and Hamas still chose October 7. Erase the power, call the weaker party an instinct, then accuse the other side of the automaton story. That is the projection.

1948 is the same edit. A UN vote the Palestinians did not cast handed most of the country to a minority. The Arab states rejected it and went to war. The war is not the alibi. Lydda and Ramle were emptied by force, villages were razed, and the refugees were barred from return. Born of war, not by design, is a comfort line pasted over the expulsions.

Olmert’s offer was a verbal sketch, never signed, with Israel keeping the valley, the water, and an army on the border. That is not a state. Settlements grew through every round. They were offered a map. What was withheld was a border they controlled.

On shields he quoted the half that licenses him. Using civilians as cover is a crime. It does not erase the duty to distinguish and to stop when the civilian dead dwarf the gain. Not a veto is his paraphrase, doing the work of a permit. A toll of 74,228 is the test.

On trials, an opened file is not a court. The Rafah medics and the Hind Rajab ambulance are folders inside the army that killed them. Hamas tried none of its men for October 7. That stains Hamas. It does not make a child or a medic guilty of what those men did. If civilians answer for their rulers, every Israeli is fair game for the occupation, the settlements, and the prime minister who funded Hamas to block a state. He will not take that rule. He only uses it on the people who cannot vote for the government bombing them.

Surveillance can facilitate human rights abuses and even genocide
There is a long history of data about sensitive attributes being misused, including the use of the 1940 USA Census to intern Japanese Americans, a system of identity cards introduced by the Belgian colonial government that were later used during the 1994 Rwandan genocide (in which nearly a million people were murdered), and the role of IBM in helping Nazi Germany use punchcard computers to identify and track the mass killing of millions of Jewish people. More recently, the mass internment of over one million people who are part of an ethnic minority in Western China was facilitated through the use of a surveillance network of cameras, biometric data (including images of people’s faces, audio of their voices, and blood samples), and phone monitoring.

Adolf Hitler meeting with IBM CEO Tom Watson Sr. in 1937. Source: Computer History
Pictured above is Adolf Hitler (far left) meeting with IBM CEO Tom Watson Sr. (2nd from left), shortly before Hitler awarded Watson a special “Service to the Reich” medal in 1937 (for a timeline of the Holocaust, see here). Watson returned the medal in 1940, although IBM continued to do business with the Nazis. IBM technology helped the Nazis conduct detailed censuses in countries they occupied, to thoroughly identify anyone of Jewish descent. Nazi concentration camps used IBM’s punchcard machines to tabulate prisoners, recording whether they were Jewish, gay, or Gypsies, and whether they died of “natural causes,” execution, suicide, or via “special treatment” in gas chambers. It is not the case that IBM sold the machines and then was done with it. Rather, IBM and its subsidiaries provided regular training and maintenance on-site at the concentration camps: printing off cards, configuring machines, and repairing them as they broke frequently.

Data is often used for different purposes than why it was collected
In the above examples, the data collection began before genocide was committed. IBM began selling to Nazi Germany well before the Holocaust (although continued for far too long), including helping with Germany’s 1933 census conducted by Adolf Hitler, which was effective at identifying far more Jewish people than had previously been recognized in Germany.

It is important to recognize how data and images gathered through surveillance can be weaponized later. Columbia professor Tim Wu wrote that “One [hard truth] is that data and surveillance networks created for one purpose can and will be used for others. You must assume that any personal data that Facebook or Android keeps are data that governments around the world will try to get or that thieves will try to steal.”

Plenty of data collection is not involved with such extreme abuse as genocide; however, in a time of global resurgence of white supremacist, ethno-nationalist, and authoritarian movements, it would be deeply irresponsible to not consider how data & surveillance can and will be weaponized against already vulnerable groups.

Data often has errors (and no mechanism for correcting them)
A database of suspected gang members maintained by California law enforcement officials was found to be full of errors, including 42 babies who had been added to the database when they were less than 1 year old (28 of whom were marked as “admitting to being gang members”). Even worse, there was no process in place for correcting mistakes or removing people once they’ve been added.

An NPR reporter recounts his experience of trying to rent an apartment and discovering that TransUnion, one of the 3 major credit bureaus, incorrectly reported him as having two felony firearms convictions. TransUnion only removed the mistakes after a dozen phone calls and notification that the story would be reported on. This is not an unusual story: the FTC’s large-scale study of credit reports in 2012 found 26% of consumers had at least one mistake in their files and 5% had errors that could be devastating. An even more opaque, unregulated “4th bureau” exists: a collection of companies buying and selling personal information about people on the margins of the banking system (such as immigrants, students, and people with low incomes), with no standards on what types of data are included, no way to opt out, and no system for identifying or correcting mistakes.

Surveillance typically operates with no accountability
What makes the examples in the previous section disturbing is not just that errors occurred, but that there was no way to identify or correct them, and no accountability for those profiting off the error-laden data. Often, even the existence of the systems being used is not publicly known (much less details of how these systems work), unless discovered by journalists or revealed by whistleblowers. The Detroit Police Dept used facial recognition technology for nearly two years without public input and in violation of a requirement that a policy be approved by the city’s Board of Police Commissioners, until a study from Georgetown Law’s Center for Privacy & Technology drew attention to the issue. Palantir, the defense startup founded by billionaire Peter Thiel, ran a program with New Orleans Police Department for 6 years which city council members did not even know about, much less have any oversight.

After two studies found that Amazon’s facial recognition software produced inaccurate and racially biased results, Amazon countered that the researchers should have changed the default parameters. However, it turned out that Amazon was not instructing police departments that use its software to do this either. Surveillance programs are operating with few regulations, no oversight, no accountability around accuracy or mistakes, and in many cases, no public knowledge of what is going on.

Surveillance changes our behavior
Hundreds of thousands of people in Hong Kong are protesting an unpopular new bill which would allow extradition to China. Typically, Hong Kong locals use their rechargeable smart cards to ride the subway. However, during the protests, long lines of people waited to use cash to buy paper tickets (usually something that only tourists do) concerned that they would be tracked for having attended the protests. Would fewer people protest if this was not an option?

In the United States, in 2015 the Baltimore Police Department used facial recognition technology to surveil people protesting the death of Freddie Grey, a young Black man who was killed in police custody, and arrested protesters with outstanding warrants. Mass surveillance could have a chilling impact on our rights to move about freely, to express ourselves, and to protest. “We act differently when we know we are ‘on the record.’ Mass privacy is the freedom to act without being watched and thus in a sense, to be who we really are,” Columbia professor Tim Wu wrote in the New York Times.

Flyer from the company Geofeedia Source
Surveillance disproportionately impacts those who are already marginalized
Surveillance is applied unevenly, causing the greatest harm to people who are already marginalized, including immigrants, people of color, and people living in poverty. These groups are more heavily policed and surveilled. The Perpetual Line-Up from the Georgetown Law Center on Privacy and Technology studied the unregulated use of facial recognition by police, with half of all Americans appearing in law enforcement databases, and the risks of errors, racial bias, misuses, and threats to civil liberties. The researchers pointed out that African Americans are more likely to appear in these databases (many of which are drawn from mug shots) since they are disproportionately likely to be stopped, interrogated, or arrested. For another example, consider the contrast between how easily people over 65 can apply for Medicare benefits by filling out an online form, with the invasive personal questions asked of a low-income mother on Medicaid about her lovers, hygiene, parental shortcomings, and personal habits.

In an article titled Trading privacy for survival is another tax on the poor, Ciara Byrne wrote, “Current public benefits programs ask applicants extremely detailed and personal questions and sometimes mandate home visits, drug tests, fingerprinting, and collection of biometric information… Employers of low-income workers listen to phone calls, conduct drug tests, monitor closed-circuit television, and require psychometric tests as conditions of employment. Prisoners in some states have to consent to be voiceprinted in order to make phone calls.”

Data privacy is a public good, like air quality or safe drinking water
Data is more revealing in aggregate. It can be nearly impossible to know what your individual data could reveal when combined with the data of others or with data from other sources, or when machine learning inference is performed on it. For instance, as Zeynep Tufekci wrote in the New York Times, individual Strava users could not have predicted how in aggregate their data could be used to identify the locations of US military bases. “Data privacy is not like a consumer good, where you click ‘I accept’ and all is well. Data privacy is more like air quality or safe drinking water, a public good that cannot be effectively regulated by trusting in the wisdom of millions of individual choices. A more collective response is needed.”

Unfortunately, this also means that you can’t fully safeguard your privacy on your own. You may choose not to purchase Amazon’s ring doorbell, yet you can still show up in the video footage collected by others. You might strengthen your online privacy practices, yet conclusions will still be inferred about you based on the behavior of others. As Professor Tufekci wrote, we need a collective response.

We don’t have to accept invasive surveillance
Many people are uncomfortable with surveillance, but feel like they have no say in the matter. While the threats surveillance poses are large, it is not too late to act. We are seeing success: in response to community organizing and an audit, Los Angeles Police Department scrapped a controversial program to predict who is most likely to commit violent crimes. Citizens, researchers, and activists in Detroit have been effective at drawing attention to the Detroit Police Department’s unregulated use of facial recognition and a bill calling for a 5-year moratorium has been introduced to the state legislature. Local governments in San Francisco, Oakland, and Somerville have banned the use of facial recognition by police.

For further resources, please check out: - Georgetown Law Center on Privacy and Technology - Digital Defense Playbook
8 Things You Need to Know about Surveillance

text:
The British school dinner was invented by the army, after it tried to recruit for a war and found the country's young men too stunted to send.

In 1899 Britain went to war in South Africa and called for volunteers. In Manchester 11,000 men came forward. The army doctors sent 8,000 of them home. They were too short, too thin, with bad chests, rotten teeth and legs bent by rickets. The minimum height had already been cut to five feet.

A general wrote it up in a magazine under the title Where to Get Men. He put it plainly. Three out of five who offered themselves were unfit to carry a rifle.

Parliament panicked. It set up a Committee on Physical Deterioration, which toured the slums and reported in 1904. Its finding was that the men had been ruined as children, by hunger, and that no amount of drill would fix at eighteen what had not been fed at eight.

It recommended that the state give hungry children a hot meal at school.

The Act passed in 1906. Within a generation there was a cooked dinner of meat and a pudding in nearly every school in the land.

So the stew, the mince, the liver and the jam roly-poly were a defence measure. The Empire had looked at the children it would need in ten years and concluded it was cheaper to feed them now.

Today the army is turning recruits away for being too heavy. Nobody has set up a committee.

The recipe is simple. Deliver whatever is cheap and easy. Blame "market conditions" and "partner delays" for anything serious. And in between, keep reminding everyone how hard you work. We keep our word. We DELIVER.
Like one voice in a ethereum:0x95af4af910c28e8ece4512bfe46f1f33687424ce Space said: "Where have you ever seen a team that delivered this much? You should appreciate it."
I do. Let me show you how much.
Roadmap Q4 2025, delivered:
🔶 Major boxing sponsorship
🔶 Soccer Academy sponsorship
The boxing.
Dec 3: "a big PBC boxing event in Texas… on Amazon Prime… the Manyu logo will be displayed on his trunks."
Dec 5: "huge viewership", "a blueprint for how crypto can scale with integrity, purpose, and impact". And my favourite: "turn a meme into a legacy".
What actually happened.
The fight was on the free prelims, before the main show even started.
Manyu was one patch out of six on those trunks. Sharing the space with "Los Valenzuela Tire Shop 2 LLC" (suspension, brakes, oil change, new & used tires, it's all printed on the patch) and "Aftermath Addiction Treatment Center".
Our guy was on the canvas 57 seconds into round one. In round eight the ref stopped it with one second left on the clock.
They even got his record wrong. 30-5, they said. It was 31-5.
Major.
The soccer academy.
"Equipping the academy of young footballers with Manyu-branded uniforms."
The academy has no name. There is no photo of the team. What we got is a 3D render of a jacket from a uniform shop in Maracaibo, with the shop's phone number at the bottom and a Bible verse on the back: "Put all your works in the hands of the Lord, and your plans will succeed." Proverbs 16:3.
Honestly the best roadmap advice they ever posted.
Beautiful design, no argument there. Did anyone see a single kid wearing it? I must have missed it.
And yes, Venezuela again. Venezuelan academy, uniform shop in Maracaibo. Nobody wonders why Venezuela keeps popping up? You're not connecting enough dots. I am 🙂

Now the part that isn't funny.
The week before the "major sponsorships", the launch bundle went quiet. 2 sales, 0.08 ETH. In the two weeks before that they were selling around 915B MANYU a day.
Then the first post went out, and the bundle sold every single day for 18 days straight.
9 hours after the boxing post, a launch-bundle wallet sold 273B.
Fight night, a wallet that got its MANYU from that same bundle wallet sold 5 times between 20:40 and 01:35 UTC. Busy night for everyone.
Dec 3 to Dec 20: 6.5T MANYU sold for 22.9 ETH, plus 750B sent to an exchange.
Ten days after the first post, the price was 20% below where it stood the night before.

So that's the business model, the way I see it. Announce something tiny. Call it major. Let the hype bring the buyers in. Let the bundle meet them at the door. Repeat.

text:
I read a post from a parent enjoying their teen’s “I’m a COMMUNIST now!” phase despite not being a communist themselves. 

I thought this was a joke in the style of “my cat is a communist — takes what it needs, gives what it wants” but reading the replies made me realize it wasn’t. 

Kids who say this can be wonderful and smart. Finding an extreme creed that will be controversial with adults is a typical edgy teenage thing to do. 

But I would still draw a line at normalizing it even though I would stop well short of trying to coerce them into accepting my way of thinking. 

It might well turn out that the teen is using communism as a label for something most of us would call a social democracy. It is very much worth separating these good ideas from communism and insisting they not be equated. 

Communism as an ideology is dangerous precisely because it carries some good ideas that can be very seductive while urging toward action whose implementation tends to become violent no matter what nice communist academics assert. That has always been the experience with regimes founded on that ideology, if for no other reason than it demands the abolition of private property, which holders of said property tend to find objectionable. 

Every doctrine can be twisted into a violent purge of its opponents but utopian ones are especially prone to that because these costs can be portrayed as necessary for the bright future that’s just around the corner.

Capitalism, for example, does not offer anything like that. People denigrate it because it seems to be all about crass profit and consumerism, but I think that its inability to provide a coherent ideological core for mass mobilization is one of its greatest strengths. It’s boring, and this is great — each of us can decide what groups to join, how to socialize, and so different communities can make different choices, giving us both ideological and de facto diversity even within the same state.

You can’t get personal liberty in a regime dedicated to a utopian future where sacrifice of individuals for the common good is routine. It’s no coincidence that capitalism is a foundational requirement for individual freedom that most classical liberals emphasize. 

Christianity has a lot of good ideas too, and they do not require you to believe in its God. I have two kids who both know that I’m an avowed atheist. Yet my daughter occasionally goes to church with her friends and their families — and all I told her was to dress appropriately instead of showing up with a bare midriff. My son joined some school group that offers treats in exchange for telling bible stories or something — I am not banning this either. But in both cases I have had a talk with them to make sure they understand what the purpose of these groups is and what I think about their goals. 

The teens will decide for themselves but I absolutely want them to know what they would be buying into. Especially if the ideas that do not require belief in the Christian God are, in fact, good and admirable. I don’t want the belief smuggled in among the beautiful things surrounding it. 

We can’t just brush aside the reality that whenever a regime implements communism, somehow it ends very high up on the scale of murdering its own citizens. This empirical regularity suggests that at the very least there’s something at the core of that ideology that makes it easy to use to justify these practices. Being aware of that and looking for alternatives to get at some of the good goals is totally worth it. 

It’s not just appropriate but it’s very much desirable to talk about the distribution of costs and benefits in society — a political rather than a purely economic matter — and work toward various remedies for unfair or unjust outcomes. None of that requires the abolition of private property.

text:
Galatians 5:16 Commentary
1. Verse Quoted in KJV
“This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” Galatians 5:16
2. Detailed Exegesis of Each Natural Phrase
“This I say then,”
Paul begins with “This I say then,” tying verse 16 directly to everything he has just written about Christian liberty, love, and destructive fleshly conflict. Verse 13 warned believers not to use liberty “for an occasion to the flesh.” Verse 14 commanded love toward one’s neighbour, and verse 15 warned that Christians can “bite and devour one another” until they consume each other. Now Paul supplies the positive answer. He does not merely say, “Stop fighting,” “Try harder,” or “Develop better manners.” He goes beneath the behaviour to the governing power: “Walk in the Spirit.”
The word “then” therefore carries doctrinal weight. Paul has rejected legal bondage as the means of producing righteousness, but that does not leave the Christian without power for holy living. Legalism always asks, “If you remove the law as the believer’s governing system, what will keep him from sin?” Paul answers with the Holy Spirit. The Christian is not transferred from law to lawlessness but from external bondage to inward spiritual life. Grace does not remove the engine and tell the car to coast downhill; God places His Spirit within the believer and tells him how to walk.
That destroys the false choice between legalism and carnality. The Bible offers neither. Legalism trusts flesh to become righteous through regulation; carnality simply lets flesh run loose. Paul gives a third and biblical answer: the Spirit governs the walk. The believer’s liberty therefore is neither bondage beneath Sinai nor independence from God. It is freedom to live from the new life God has supplied in Christ.
“Walk in the Spirit,”
The command is “Walk in the Spirit.” Walking is ordinary, continual, practical movement. Paul does not say, “Visit the Spirit occasionally,” or “Have one spectacular spiritual experience and live on the memory for twenty years.” A walk is composed of repeated steps. Christian spirituality is therefore not merely measured by extraordinary moments at an altar, emotional intensity, public ministry, or unusual experiences. It is revealed in the steady direction of daily life.
To walk in the Spirit presupposes that the believer possesses the Spirit. Galatians 4:6 says, “because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts.” Romans 8:9 says, “if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.” The command is addressed to people already indwelt by the Holy Ghost. Paul is not teaching them how to obtain the Spirit through lawkeeping; Galatians 3:2 has already reminded them that they received the Spirit “by the hearing of faith.” Christian conduct flows from an indwelling already given by grace.
Walking in the Spirit also means living under His influence in agreement with the word He inspired. The Holy Ghost does not lead believers contrary to Scripture and then ask them to call the contradiction “spiritual.” Ephesians 5:18 commands, “be filled with the Spirit,” while Colossians 3:16 says, “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly.” The results in those passages run remarkably together because Spirit-filled living and Scripture-saturated living are not enemies. The Holy Ghost who wrote the Book has no secret ministry of contradicting it after publication.
Practically, walking in the Spirit touches decisions, attitudes, reactions, speech, priorities, relationships, thoughts, appetites, and service. When insulted, will flesh retaliate or will the Spirit govern? When tempted, will flesh negotiate or will Scripture be obeyed? When praised, will flesh inflate? When ignored, will flesh sulk? The Spirit-filled walk becomes visible in ordinary intersections where Adam wants the steering wheel.
“and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.”

text:
A BANK NOW MARKS DOWN DEUTSCHE TELEKOM $DTEGY FOR A DEAL IT HAS NOT ANNOUNCED:

Deutsche Telekom (DTEGY) at $29.82, +$0.62 / +2.12% on Friday.

- Since the quoted post, from the September 18 close of $31.27: -$1.45 / -4.6%.
- In Frankfurt: 26.56 euros at Friday's close, vs 27.38 on September 18, -3.0%. The US line also carries the euro.

The quoted post said the company had done nothing to earn its fall. On September 25, Bernstein cut its rating on Deutsche Telekom itself, and its sharpest reason is a deal nobody has announced: Deutsche Telekom buying the rest of T-Mobile US with new shares of its own. The verdict: Deutsche Telekom is now marked down for its own open questions, and the price fell hardest on the days bond yields rose, the one half of the quoted post that held up.

First, the grade. The quoted post missed three things.

- It called the company blameless and never mentioned the T-Mobile question, though it was already public. On September 2, Bloomberg reported that Elliott Investment Management, an activist fund that buys stakes to push companies to change course, had built a stake in Deutsche Telekom and wanted it to drop chief executive Tim Hoettges' push to buy out T-Mobile US.
- The dividend is 1.00 euro a share, set at the April 1 annual meeting, not the 1.138 euros it printed.
- It said the company could not answer with anything of its own until November 5. An investor day in Bonn, this Monday, was already on the calendar.

What Bernstein wrote on September 25:

- Rating: cut to market-perform, meaning own about as much of it as the market does, from outperform.
- Target: 28.10 euros, from 37. Friday's close sits below even the lowered target.
- German broadband revenue growth: 1.7% in the first half of 2026, vs 4.5% in the second half of 2023, as rival fiber networks compete harder.
- The deal math: if Deutsche Telekom paid T-Mobile US's outside holders a 20% premium in new shares, current owners would be diluted about 11%, each share owning a smaller slice, and former T-Mobile holders would own about 42% of the combined company.

That last line runs against what the company does with its cash today. This year Deutsche Telekom is spending as much as 5 billion euros, about 4% of its market value, buying back its own shares. The deal Bernstein modeled would go the other way, issuing enough new shares to hand 42% of the company to outsiders.

Germany got an answer of its own on October 1: Deutsche Telekom raised monthly prices by about 1 euro on most home broadband plans, for new customers only. A higher price for new customers adds revenue only if rival fiber networks do not sign them up first.

The US line did not fall on the note. It closed up 0.8% that day, at $30.90. The drop came over the next four sessions, as bond yields climbed:

- US line: $29.20 on Thursday, -5.5% from that close.
- 10-year Treasury yield, what Washington pays to borrow for ten years: 5.17% on September 25, as high as 5.29% on September 30.

Friday won back 2.1%.

T-Mobile US (TMUS) at $163.64, +$1.91 / +1.18% on Friday.

- Since the September 18 close of $168.18: -$4.54 / -2.7%.
- During Friday's session it touched $160.81, its lowest price in a year.

What that does to the parent, in dollars:

- Deutsche Telekom's stake of about 54%: roughly $95B.
- Deutsche Telekom's own market value: $145.5B.
- Left for everything else, the German network included: about $51B, vs about $54B on the quoted post's math.

The rest of the company fell faster than the American stake. T-Mobile US fits none of the six Len5es: a stock at a one-year low is the opposite of the climb Momentum wants, and at about 17 times profit with a 2.5% dividend it offers neither the discount the value Len5es hunt nor the payout Income favors.

Deutsche Telekom is still a pick on none of the six Len5es. Income stays the nearest: it hunts cash reaching owners that the business itself pays for. The quoted post set the test, a lower price lifting the yield, and the test ran backwards:

- Dividend yield, 1.00 euro on the Frankfurt price: about 3.7% on September 18, 3.8% on Friday.
- 10-year Treasury: 5.01% on September 18, 5.28% on Friday.

The price fell and the yield rose, but the bond rose faster, so the gap widened. What would put Deutsche Telekom on the Income Len5: a 2026 dividend big enough to close that gap, with no share-paid deal shrinking each owner's slice. The board proposes it with full-year results on Thursday, February 25, 2027.

The dates before that:

- Monday, October 5: the AI investor day in Bonn, the first time management faces investors since the note. The agenda is artificial intelligence, and the merger may not come up.
- Thursday, November 5: third-quarter results. The number that settles the German half is broadband growth against that 1.7%, beside the 47.5 billion euro forecast for profit before interest, tax and equipment wear.

The risk is the deal itself: an offer for T-Mobile US paid in Deutsche Telekom shares would turn Bernstein's 42% from a model into a fact.

The quoted post asked why a company with a raised forecast was being sold. The question that mattered was what Deutsche Telekom would pay for the rest of T-Mobile US, and whether in cash or in new shares.

Not investment advice.

text:
Every triumph and tragedy in human history, the blood-soaked battlefields of ancient wars, the soaring symphonies of Beethoven, the quiet ache of unrequited love, even the raw edge of personal suffering, reduced to nothing more than a cosmic grocery list..!.

Not the epic saga of our spiritual climb, but a mere tally of sustenance for that pale, indifferent orb glowing in the night sky.

The Moon, in this view, is a voracious entity, and we're its unwitting farm...

This is the provocative heart of the teachings from George Ivanovich Gurdjieff, a 20th-century mystic whose ideas still rattle cages in philosophy, spirituality, and even science today.

Gurdjieff's "lunar cosmology" flips our self-aggrandizing worldview on its head.

It suggests a humiliating cosmic pecking order where humanity isn't the pinnacle of creation but a cog in a vast, impersonal machine.

And the wild part?

Decades after his death, elements of his esoteric visions are finding unexpected echoes in modern astrophysics, biology, and planetary science.

Who was George Gurdjieff? - The Enigmatic Mystic behind the Moon Theory

To grasp the weight of Gurdjieff's ideas, you have to start with the man himself - a figure as elusive as a shadow in the moonlight.

Born around 1866-1877 in Alexandropol (now Gyumri, Armenia) under the Russian Empire, Gurdjieff grew up in a melting pot of cultures.His father was Greek, a bardic poet who recited ancient epics, and his mother was Armenian (or possibly Greek, depending on the source).Fluent in Armenian, Pontic Greek, Russian, and Turkish, young Gurdjieff was steeped in diverse traditions from the get-go.

Local priests and storytellers sparked his early fascination with hidden truths beyond science or conventional religion.

📷

By his twenties, Gurdjieff embarked on epic journeys across Central Asia, Egypt, Iran, India, and Tibet, seeking esoteric knowledge from Sufis, yogis, and secret societies.

He claimed to have uncovered fragments of an ancient wisdom system, piecing them together into what he'd later call the "Fourth Way."

Settling in Russia around 1912, he gathered students like the philosopher P.D. Ouspensky, who helped spread his teachings (The Fourth Way).

After the Bolshevik Revolution, Gurdjieff fled to Europe, establishing the Institute for the Harmonious Development of Man in France in 1922.

There, he taught through lectures, music, sacred dances, and grueling physical labor, anything to jolt people from their "waking sleep."

Gurdjieff wasn't your typical guru.

He composed music with Thomas de Hartmann, wrote cryptic books like Beelzebub's Tales to His Grandson, and even dabbled in business ventures.

His methods were tough love:

"Stop" exercises to freeze mid-action for self-observation, or tasks designed to expose ego.

He died in 1949, but his legacy lives on through foundations worldwide.

Critics called him a charlatan; devotees, a genius.

Either way, his cosmology - especially the Moon bit - remains one of his most shocking contributions.

What drove him?

A deep conviction that humanity is mechanically asleep, programmed like biorobots, squandering our potential.

His lunar theory isn't just cosmic trivia:

it's a wake-up call wrapped in metaphor, or is it...?

The Core of Gurdjieff's Lunar Cosmology - Humanity as 'Cosmic Livestock'

At the heart of Gurdjieff's worldview is a stark, unflinching declaration:

"The Moon is the great enemy of man.We serve the Moon. We are like sheep that she raises, feeds, shears, and saves for her own personal use. But when she is hungry, she kills as much as she wants.All organic life works for the Moon."

Chilling, right...?

This isn't poetry; it's the linchpin of his cosmic hierarchy.

In Gurdjieff's system, outlined in Beelzebub's Tales and elaborated by Ouspensky in In Search of the Miraculous, the universe unfolds through a "Ray of Creation", a descending scale from the Absolute (pure unity) down through galaxies, stars, planets, and finally, the Moon.

The Earth and Moon are locked in a brutal symbiosis.The Moon, born from a catastrophic cosmic mishap, is a "sub-planet," an immature entity struggling to https://t.co/5lE4KtsY8U sustain itself, it relies on Earth to generate a massive biological battery:
organic life.

Us? We're part of that battery...

Humans, animals, plants, we absorb solar and terrestrial energies, then transmute them via our joys, pains, and deaths into "vibrations" or subtle ethers (loosh).

These are cosmic nourishment that the Moon devours...

Our wars? Emotional flare-ups that crank the energy https://t.co/O9dmvykAWb and love? Byproducts of the churn.Creativity? Just steam from the engine.

It's a global conveyor belt where,

suffering amps up the "food" production, think mass tragedies as bumper harvests...

The Ray of Creation - A Cosmic Food Chain

Dig deeper into the Ray.

Gurdjieff borrowed from ancient sources, blending them with pseudo-scientific flair.

The Absolute emanates worlds in octaves, like musical scales, governed by laws: three at the top (unity), ballooning to 96 at the Moon (chaos).Organic life bridges a gap in this chain, transforming coarse matter into finer substances.

The Moon, as the Ray's endpoint, is a "growing branch," a fetal world feeding off Earth's output...

Remove life, and the whole system stalls.

📷

Ouspensky likened the Moon to a clock's weight:

"Organic life is clockwork... If the kettlebell is removed, the movement will stop immediately."

It's elegant, almost logical, if you squint past the mysticism.

But Gurdjieff insisted this isn't allegory.

The Moon is alive, evolving, and we're its sustenance...!

Troubling? Absolutely...

Yet it forces a rethink:

Are we masters of fate, or glorified space cattle...?

Prophecy in Myth - Gurdjieff's Eerie foresight on the Moon's Birth

Here's where it gets downright spooky.

In Beelzebub's Tales, Gurdjieff spins a yarn about the young Earth's collision with a comet called Kondur (or Komdoor).

The impact shears off two chunks:

the big one becomes the Moon
the small one, a forgotten satellite called Anulios

In the early 1900s, this was dismissed as wild myth.

Scientists favored gentler ideas, like the Moon budding from Earth or getting captured by gravity.

📷

Fast-forward to the late 20th century, and bam...,

the scientific consensus shifts to the Giant Impact Hypothesis.

Around 4.5 billion years ago, a Mars-sized protoplanet dubbed Theia slammed into proto-Earth.

Debris coalesced into the Moon...

Gurdjieff nailed the catastrophic origin, even if he called it a comet instead of a planet.

He was decades ahead...

Latest Twists in Moon formation Science

Science hasn't stood still.

Recent updates refine this tale...

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) research pushes the impact back to about 4.25 billion years ago, 300 million years earlier than thought, rewriting lunar history.

Simulations suggest a glancing blow vaporized rock at 10,000°C, explaining the Moon's tiny iron core and volatile-poor composition.

In 2023, models proposed Theia's remnants lurk inside Earth as massive mantle blobs, detectable via seismic waves.

A 2022 study shows such impacts can fling a Moon-mass body into stable orbit instantly, solving isotopic puzzles, Earth and Moon share near-identical oxygen and titanium fingerprints.

Even lunar rust mysteries tie in:

2025 research links it to Earth's atmospheric "wind" carrying oxygen.

And Apollo 17 rocks? They're now connected to the Sea of Serenity's birth, hinting at volcanic timelines.

Gurdjieff's "prophecy" wasn't perfect -  no Anulios found yet - but it's uncannily close.

Was he tapping ancient lore, or something deeper...?

Gravity's Grip - The Moon's tangible hold on Earthly Life

Gurdjieff's chain isn't just ethereal:

it's gravitational.

Without the Moon, Earth's axis wobbles wildly, erasing seasons.

Tides, lunar-driven, may have birthed life in primordial soups.

Cycles influence everything: human sleep, animal migrations, plant growth.

Lunar Rhythms in Biology and Behavior

Studies show lunar phases sync with fertility, menstruation, and birth rates - melatonin dips under full moons.Animals?
Corals spawn en masse; wolves howl more.Even humans:
2024 research ties moon cycles to health, debunking "lunacy" myths while affirming subtle effects.The impact may have homogenized Earth's carbon, enabling autotrophic life origins.

Is this the "subtle exchange" Gurdjieff meant?
Science says gravity stabilizes our biosphere; he hinted at energies beyond.Without the Moon, life might not exist - or it'd be alien...

Beyond the Physical - Vibrations, Fields, and Speculative Parallels

Gurdjieff's "vibrations" sound woo-woo, but consider:

Modern physics talks quantum fields, entanglement.

A 2025 paper reframes his Moon as "recursive emergence" in a word-inhabited cosmos, blending Logos theology with cosmology.

Morphic resonance (Rupert Sheldrake) or Akashic fields echo his ideas - collective memory as cosmic food?

📷

Critics slam it as anti-science:

The Moon's "cold, lifeless," per astronomy...

Yet parallels persist - his hydrogen atom hints predated subatomic discoveries.

The Fourth Way - Breaking Free from Lunar Bondage

Why this grim cosmology? It's Gurdjieff's alarm clock.

We live in "waking sleep," mechanical puppets. The Fourth Way offers escape: Work on all centers - body, emotions, mind - simultaneously, sans monastery.

Key Principles for Awakening
Self-Observation: Watch yourself like a stranger.
Conscious Labor: Do tasks fully present.
Intentional Suffering: Endure ego hits.
The Many 'I's': Unify your fractured self.
Laws of Three and Seven: Navigate life's octaves.Through movements, music, and effort, awaken to create your soul.

The Ultimate Wake-Up Call - Liberation in Understanding

Repulsive as "food for the Moon" is, it's a ego-shatterer.

Understand the chains, and freedom beckons

Gurdjieff's revelation? Consolation in clarity.Who are we?What drives us?

The Fourth Way says:

"Awake", and decide...!
