The law states that a person commits an offence if they knowingly offer or agree to pay a fee to another person for the purpose of engaging in s+xual conduct.

A first offence can attract 180 days to two years in a state jail facility and a fine of up to $10,000, while a second offence carries two to 10 years in prison and up to a $10,000 fine.

Reports say Okerie and Ezeikwe could therefore face up to 10 years in prison and a $10,000 fine, depending on the category of the alleged offences.

🚨Secunderabad Army Arms Theft: 7 More Arrested, Including 3 Serving Personnel

Telangana Police have arrested seven more people, taking the total accused in the case to eight, after weapons and ammunition were stolen from the 20 Battalion, Madras Regiment armoury at Bolarum, Secunderabad Cantonment, on August 30. The prime accused, retired Havildar Upputholla Mallesh alias Raju, was arrested on September 11. 

Those arrested in the latest round:
Konduri Sheshulu, 36 — Sepoy
Vinod Kumar, 34 — Naik/Jawan and Kote employee
Kucharakanthi Praveen, 37 — Havildar
Avi Dey alias Obi, 32 — West Bengal
Birbal Shaw, 27 — West Bengal
Upputholla Mallikarjun, 39 — Mallesh’s cousin
Chemmakar Niranjan, 39 — Mallesh’s friend

Police allege the three serving personnel helped Mallesh break open the Kote and Magazine and remove the weapons. All seven were subsequently sent to judicial custody. 

🔫 What Was Stolen?
Police recovered military weapons and ammunition including four AK-203 rifles, an INSAS rifle and six 9mm pistols, along with magazines and large quantities of ammunition. Reports differ on some inventory details, but authorities said the stolen military cache was recovered. 

💰 Alleged Robbery Plan
According to Malkajgiri Police Commissioner B. Sumathi, Mallesh, his cousin and Niranjan allegedly planned to use firearms for bank, jewellery-shop and wealthy-person robberies. Investigators allege they also planned to sell some stolen Army weapons in West Bengal.

Police say potential buyers allegedly offered ₹3 lakh for each pistol and ₹5 lakh for each long weapon, plus payment for ammunition.

text:
REN REACTS TO "The Most Disgusting Influencer Campaign of 2026"

The most revealing detail in the entire Polymarket saga isn't the fake wins or the sock-puppet accounts. It's that the winning trades never existed in the database. Over 100 videos showing nearly $900,000 in supposed profits — and every single one was fabricated on a dummy site called https://t.co/oelshvsWgc, where a capital I replaces the lowercase l, making it indistinguishable from https://t.co/PbqKcGbqfA on screen. The journalists spent over a week searching for these trades before someone noticed the URL. That's the whole operation in one detail: manufacture the appearance of easy money, pump it through an army of paid reposters who hide their affiliation, and let the 85% of users who lose money overall fund the house fees.

The core thesis is simple. Polymarket is a fee-extraction middleman with no skin in the game. Winners are paid by losers, not by the platform. The platform takes a cut on every trade regardless of outcome. This means Polymarket's entire incentive structure points toward one thing: volume. More users, more bets, more fees. The quality of those bets doesn't matter to the platform — but it matters enormously to the users placing them. A recent study found 85% of Polymarket traders lose money overall and only 2% have won more than $1,000 in total. The people who consistently win need the people who consistently lose. Some users even track badly performing accounts to place opposite trades. The platform needs a steady inflow of what the industry calls, with refreshing honesty, "unskilled losers."

Signals: 140+ million views on fake bet clips according to analytics provider Tubular. $2.5 million sent from a Polymarket executive's personal PayPal to over 800 people across 14 months. Creators paid $2,000–3,000/month to film fake wins and explicitly told not to disclose payment. Clippers given written guidance: if you have "poly" or "Polymarket" in your username, you won't get paid. Clippers told to use US SIM cards to appear American — despite the site being officially banned in the US since 2022. Polymarket valued at up to $15 billion. Over $100 million spent to acquire a licensed US exchange and clearinghouse in mid-2025. A consumer protection lawsuit filed citing the journalism. CFTC investigation ongoing. The supposed wins in the fake videos totaled ~$900,000; identical real bets would have lost over $160,000.

Between the lines: the "prediction market, not gambling" framing is the entire play. When a platform insists it isn't gambling while simultaneously running undisclosed paid promotions featuring fake wins to young US audiences, the gap between stated position and operational reality is the scam. Polymarket reportedly bans insider trading while also promoting itself as the most accurate source of truth on the internet — a tension that resolves when you realize informed flow is good for volume. The Maduro capture market saw a spike in bets shortly before the operation was publicly announced — timing and size flow suggest informed activity. A public figure invested in Polymarket and became an official advisor; an older CFTC investigation was dropped within half a year of the current administration taking office. The FBI raided the founder's home in 2024 under the previous administration. That regulatory pendulum is the structural wildcard.

The undisclosed ad problem is systematic, not incidental. According to reports, internal guidance allegedly instructed people not to mark tweets as paid promotions and to pretend they were organic. A Polymarket employee reportedly approached a creator who had publicly criticized the practice, acknowledged it had happened in the past, and claimed it had stopped. Multiple creators who received offers report being told they could not disclose the paid nature of the content. When the journalists reached out, many creators deleted their videos or hid their profiles. Polymarket told the Wall Street Journal it plans to conduct a "comprehensive audit" of active promotional content — a statement that implicitly concedes the problem exists while committing to nothing specific.

Risk: the primary sources are Wall Street Journal and Politico investigative reporting, which carry weight but are not legal findings. FTC disclosure rules exist but enforcement has been inconsistent. The consumer protection lawsuit and CFTC investigation are ongoing — outcomes unknown. Polymarket's statements to press are non-responsive on most specific questions. Verification hierarchy: on-chain trade data (public, verifiable) > journalist documentation with screenshots and source interviews > company statements > social media posts. The gap between on-chain reality and social media presentation is where the deception lives.

Flip: 1) CFTC investigation produces enforcement action or settlement with material penalties — shifts regulatory risk pricing. 2) Consumer protection lawsuit succeeds or forces disclosure requirements — changes the cost structure of the influencer pipeline. 3) FTC brings specific cases against undisclosed Polymarket promotions — precedent risk for all prediction market marketing. 4) Administration change re-tightens CFTC posture — the regulatory umbrella that allowed the US re-entry could close. 5) Major media partner (Yahoo Finance, Dow Jones) distances itself — legitimacy signal reverses. 6) Whistleblower from inside the marketing operation provides documented internal guidance — converts "allegedly" to "demonstrably."

Trade: the structural edge for informed participants is real but parasitic on the uninformed flow. If you're trading on Polymarket, the baseline assumption must be that promotional content is paid and undisclosed unless proven otherwise. The 85% loss rate is your prior. Volume spikes preceding major news events warrant scrutiny — if timing/size flow suggests informed activity, the retail side of that market is already underwater. The fee model means the platform has zero incentive to police its own marketing or the quality of information reaching new users. That misalignment is the trade: short the trust, long the fees.

Watch: CFTC investigation docket and any settlement terms. Consumer protection lawsuit filings and class certification. FTC enforcement actions on undisclosed influencer promotions broadly. Spread and depth on political event markets ahead of major announcements — informed flow leaves footprints in orderbook shape. Cross-market consistency: if Polymarket odds diverge from other prediction platforms without new information, someone with information is moving the line. Regulatory proposals from Congress on prediction market oversight. And always — the ratio of promotional spend to product quality. The more a platform markets, the less it builds. That heuristic has never failed.

Bottom line: Polymarket's marketing apparatus is designed to manufacture losers. Every fake win video, every undisclosed paid tweet, every sock-puppet clipper account points the same direction — toward a steady supply of new users who will lose 85% of the time and fund the platform's fee revenue. Trade accordingly, or don't trade at all.

Neither game was anywhere near as impressive as they were made out to be.

These are apparently the guys who are on PlayStation's payroll, by the way. 😂

I'm going to be real though, GEARS E-DAY looks fucking incredible. I'm not taking anything away from what The Coalition have achieved here.

But the idea that it's suddenly in some completely different league to everything else is a bit exaggerated.

There are already games that can absolutely stand toe to toe with it, and in certain areas offer better detail, fidelity or a more impressive overall visual experience.

• ALAN WAKE 2
• DEATH STRANDING 2
• HORIZON FORBIDDEN WEST

And that's the important distinction. Gears E-Day can be one of the best looking games around without being categorically ahead of every other game out there.

Death Stranding 2 is ridiculous when it comes to environmental detail, materials, character rendering and sheer scene complexity.

Alan Wake 2 remains an insane technical showcase for lighting, global illumination, volumetrics and dense environments.

And Horizon Forbidden West is still fucking nuts on console. The environments, foliage, character models, animation, water, materials and sheer density are phenomenal.

So yeah, GEARS E-DAY is incredible. Give The Coalition their flowers, because what they've achieved is seriously impressive.

But there are games from this generation that still stand above it visually. 😂

text:
Poster for the "Dream" or "Nightmare" fight, depending on your opinion of course, between former Heavyweight Champion Muhammad Ali and NBA legend Wilt Chamberlain, scheduled for October 4, 1971, at the Houston Astrodome.

The fight was originally scheduled for July 26th of 1971.

On April 21st of 1971, officials from the Astrodome scheduled a major announcement: Former titlist Muhammad Ali will fight here against Wilt Chamberlain, the basketball superstar.

The bout was four years in the making.

“This match may very well come to pass,” said Howard Cosell in 1967.

In March of 1967, the two appeared on Howard Cosell’s show on ABC to talk about a potential fight. Ali denied signing the deal then, as he pointed out that he wanted to fight a few people first before he would agree to a match.

In 1971, ABC scheduled another special segment for both Ali and Chamberlain to promote the fight after the former finally agreed to the NBA star’s challenge after a significant upgrade in the money they’d receive.

 On the day of the press conference, Ali waited for his opponent. But things fell apart after a pre-conference meeting.

Ali’s loss to Heavyweight Champion Joe Frazier, in March of 1971, also placed his fight with Chamberlain in jeopardy. 

Chamberlain’s goal was more than just to beat the man, he coveted what was once considered the greatest prize in all sports: the status of being The Heavyweight Champion of the World. 

Prior to the Ali-Frazier fight, Wilt had agreed that he would enter the ring after Ali defeated Frazier in March and was again champion. When Smokin’ Joe retained the title by beating Ali, the latter’s proposed fight with Chamberlain no longer carried title implications, and Wilt’s desire started to wane. Nevertheless, an intrepid former US Department of Justice Attorney named Bob Arum continued to stay in contact with Chamberlain and stoke his interest.

Although Chamberlain had no competitive experience oin the ring, he approached the Ali fight with a plan. He would retain the services of Cus D’Amato, who readily volunteered to prepare Chamberlain for the bout.

Wilt Chamberlain wasn't the first famous athlete outside of boxing to entertain a challenge of Ali.

While Ali was preparing for a fight in London in 1966, football legend Jim Brown was in the area working on the film “The Dirty Dozen”. Brown informed Bob Arum, with whom he was acquainted, that he wanted to challenge Ali to a fight for the title. 

When Ali heard this, he instructed Arum to have Brown meet him in Hyde Park where Ali took his morning training runs. 

When Brown arrived, Ali told the NFL star to try and hit him and not worry about whether Ali got hurt. Brown proceeded to throw a barrage of heavy punches, all of which Ali dodged with ease. With Brown still swinging in earnest, Ali playfully slapped Brown’s face repeatedly as the latter’s punches sailed by in futility. Brown quietly dropped his challenge thereafter.

On April 22nd of1971, Walter Cronkite reported on the CBS Evening News that Chamberlain had declined to sign the final contract for the match.

The official reason for Wilt’s withdrawal, provided by his attorneys, was that the after-tax money he'd earn from the bout was only $500,000. They claimed this was too small a purse to make the effort worthwhile. 

Naturally, other opinions abounded. 

Bob Arum believed that Wilt was trying to use the idea of the fight (and the potential that he might be injured) as leverage in contract negotiations with Los Angeles Lakers owner Jack Kent Cooke.

When interviewed in many years later, Chamberlain offered another explanation for his decision to withdraw from the fight. 

Wilt reminisced: “I remember leaving my place in L.A. and — my father is a big fight fan — and I said, `Dad, I got a couple of days off and I’m getting ready to go to Houston to sign to fight Muhammad Ali.'” His father told him he should work on his free throws instead. “And I looked at my Dad and said, ‘Well, Dad, you’re probably right.”

Trivia: Ali would instead Buster Mathis, at the Astrodome, on November 17th. Bonavena would fight Lewis, though in Buenos Aires, on October 4th as scheduled and win on a 7th round (Headbutt that opened a cut) DQ.

text:
Perk 3: Buy Back & Resell. IKEA gives you store credit for your old IKEA furniture.
 
The parents put their dining table and chairs on the curb. IKEA would have taken them.
 
Here's how it works. IKEA Family and IKEA Business Network members fill out an online quote form describing the item and its condition. IKEA emails back an estimate and a reservation number. You bring the furniture to a participating store, fully assembled. A coworker inspects it, and the final offer can differ from the online estimate depending on what they see.
 
If you accept, you get an IKEA Refund Card. The store credit doesn't expire, and it works in any US IKEA store or online.
 
The furniture then goes straight into the As-Is section for the next shopper. That's why As-Is keeps restocking.
 
What IKEA takes in the US: dressers and office drawer cabinets. Bookcases and shelf units. Sideboards and display storage. Dining tables, small tables and desks. Chairs and stools without upholstery. Children's furniture. Table and floor lamps that don't need installation.
 
What it won't take: sofas and armchairs. Anything upholstered or leather. Mattresses. Kitchens. Modular wardrobes. Appliances. Glass items. Textiles. Anything modified or "hacked." Anything that isn't IKEA.
 
It has to be fully assembled, fully working, personally used and unmodified. The credit amount depends on condition, age and functionality.
 
IKEA has expanded the program to almost 3,000 eligible items, and it runs at nearly every US store. Right now, the exceptions are Brooklyn and Houston.
 
Now do the math on the parents' dining set. The curb paid them $0. Buy Back would have paid them in store credit toward the new table they were already buying.
 
Before anything from IKEA goes to the curb, run it through the online quote form first. It costs nothing.

Here is Google on Life in Russia:
Yes, official state organizations and major financial institutions publish highly granular rankings assessing the best and worst cities in the Russian Federation. Because a mega-metropolis cannot be directly compared to a small town, these lists are strictly grouped by population size. [1]
The most authoritative metrics come from the Russian Ministry of Construction's Urban Environment Quality Index and the annual Quality of Life Index published by the Financial University under the Government of the Russian Federation. [1]
The general distribution from best to worst across the major metropolitan classes maps out as follows:
The Megacities (Population Over 1 Million)
This tier evaluates the country's 16 largest economic and political centers, grading them across categories like transport infrastructure, safety, modernization, and ecology. [1]
RankCityGeneral Breakdown & Quality Factors1MoscowThe undisputed highest-ranking city for infrastructure, digitalization, public services, and economic opportunity.2St. PetersburgConsistently takes second place, praised for high architectural integration, walkability, and strong cultural infrastructure.3KazanRegarded as the most balanced regional hub with top-tier modern residential programs, excellent IT ecosystems, and deep historical charm.4–6Nizhny Novgorod, Yekaterinburg, KrasnoyarskBalanced industrial capitals featuring massive university networks, modern river embankments, and highly active downtown cores.Bottom TierOmsk & VolgogradHistorically anchored at the absolute bottom of large-city rankings due to crumbling post-Soviet manufacturing plants, low local job markets, and lagging urban revitalization. Note: Recent state indexes show both cities are finally climbing back up to baseline acceptable scores.
Large & Medium Cities (Population Under 1 Million)
When removing the capital giants, independent and domestic rankings shift drastically toward specialized resort economies, oil wealth, or historic preservation centers. [1, 2]
The Best in Class:Tyumen: Frequently scores as the #1 regional city for quality of life. Fueled by massive oil and gas sector wealth, it features higher per-capita infrastructure spending than almost any provincial city.
Sochi & Krasnodar: Dominate southern rankings due to mild subtropical climates, massive post-Olympic infrastructure investment, and premier business flexibility.
Grozny & Kaliningrad: Highly rated for safety, clean civic centers, and distinctive pedestrian-oriented developments. [1, 2]

The Worst in Class:Yakutsk & Chita: Routinely rank near the bottom of national quality-of-life and comfort surveys. They are weighed down by severe geographic isolation, brutal sub-zero permafrost environments, outdated infrastructure networks, and extreme heating/utility maintenance costs.
Arduous Monotowns: Remote Siberian or Far East industrial cities built around single factories often carry the lowest markers for air quality, general safety, and economic retention. [1]

what percent of people live in surroundings where they could live a decent life
According to the federal standards outlined by the Ministry of Construction of the Russian Federation, approximately 60% to 70% of the urban population lives in surroundings officially classified as a "favorable urban environment". [1, 2]
The state tracks this using the Urban Environment Quality Index, which scores cities out of 360 points across 36 metrics (including safety, green spaces, transport, and public infrastructure). A city must score 181 points or higher to be considered "comfortable and favorable" for a decent life. [1, 2]
A realistic, balanced breakdown of how this translates into actual daily quality of life reveals a sharp divide:
1. The Favorable Environment Tier (60% – 70% of City Dwellers)
This group is predominantly clustered in the major economic hubs, capital sub-regions, and specialized oil or resort cities. [1]
The Mega-Hubs (~25-30%): Residents of Moscow, St. Petersburg, and wealthy capitals like Kazan enjoy world-class public transit, rapid digitization of public services, high safety indexes, and heavy investments in modern public spaces. [1, 2]
Vibrant Regional Centers (~35-40%): In places like Tyumen, Nizhny Novgorod, Yekaterinburg, and Krasnodar, infrastructure is modern enough to support a highly comfortable, stable lifestyle with reliable heating, decent healthcare, and retail ecosystems.
2. The Lagging or Struggling Tier (30% – 40% of City Dwellers)
Roughly one-third of the urban population lives in environments officially deemed "unsatisfactory" or highly stressed. [1]
Industrial Monotowns & Post-Soviet Hubs: Cities like Volgograd or Omsk have historically lagged in urban revitalization. Residents frequently deal with severe industrial air pollution, failing road networks, and fewer high-paying career paths. [1, 2]
Extreme Climatic/Isolated Peripheries: Cities in deep Siberia or the Far East (e.g., Chita or Yakutsk) struggle against brutal geographical elements. High utility maintenance costs, extreme winter freezes, and aging Soviet-era piping networks significantly lower the baseline comfort of daily life.
3. The Rural Component (Outside the Index)
While the index only tracks cities, roughly 25% of Russia's total population lives in rural areas. In these regions, a "decent life" by modern urban standards is much harder to maintain. Access to centralized gasification, reliable indoor plumbing, high-speed internet, and nearby specialized medical care drops heavily once you leave the municipal city borders. [1, 2]
If you would like, I can break down the specific criteria (like ecology, housing quality, or safety metrics) that the index uses to determine whether a city is favorable or not. [1, 2]

but some people must like the rural life - it can be bucolic
You are absolutely right. For many people, rural Russia offers an incredibly bucolic, deeply authentic, and peaceful lifestyle that no modern metropolis can replicate.
While statistical indexes focus on concrete, transit lines, and fiber-optic cables, they completely miss the rich lifestyle appeal of the Russian countryside, known locally for its profound connection to nature and traditional culture.
The Appeal of the Bucolic Russian Countryside
The Dacha Culture: Millions of urban Russians actively seek out rural life through the dacha (country house) tradition. It is a prized lifestyle centered around growing organic food, picking wild berries and mushrooms in pristine birch forests, and hosting family gatherings.
The Ultimate Escape: For those choosing to live rurally full-time, the appeal lies in the vast, open landscapes—from the rolling hills of the Golden Ring to the tranquil rivers of Siberia. It offers a slow, self-reliant pace of life free from the noise, pollution, and frantic energy of Moscow or Yekaterinburg.
Wellness and the Banya: Rural life heavily features the traditional banya (Russian sauna), clean well water, and crisp air, which many view as the ultimate recipe for physical and mental health.
The Modern "Best of Both Worlds" Trend
In recent years, the perception of rural life has shifted due to a major trend: suburbanization and remote work.
Eco-Villages and Modern Cottages: A growing class of remote workers, tech professionals, and young families are moving to modern cottage settlements (kottedzhnye posyolki) just outside major cities.
The Hybrid Lifestyle: These communities offer the best of both worlds: they are surrounded by quiet, bucolic landscapes, yet they are close enough to a highway to access high-speed internet, modern supermarkets, and city hospitals.
For those who prioritize peace, space, and a tight-knit community over city nightlife and public transit, the Russian countryside provides a uniquely beautiful and fulfilling way of live.
If you're interested, I can tell you about some of the most famous scenic villages in Russia—like Suoravda or the historic wooden villages of the North—or explain how the dacha tradition works.
so overall what percent of rural areas could be conducive to a bucolic experience
Based on a combination of infrastructure data, geographic realities, and sociodemographic research, roughly 25% to 35% of Russia’s settled rural areas are actively conducive to a comfortable, bucolic experience.
While the rustic ideal of a peaceful countryside exists, it depends heavily on location. Rural Russia is starkly divided into three distinct zones:
1. The "Bucolic & Modern" Zone (~25% – 35%)
These are the regions where the idyllic countryside lifestyle is fully realizable without sacrificing basic comfort. They are characterized by reliable access to electricity, high-speed 4G internet, and decent roads. [1]
Suburban "Dacha" Belts: Rural areas located within a 50 to 100-kilometer radius of major cities (like Moscow, St. Petersburg, Yekaterinburg, or Kazan). These host modern cottage settlements equipped with autonomous septic tanks, gasification, and grocery delivery. [1, 2, 3]
The Black Earth & Southern Agrarian Hubs: Regions like Krasnodar, Rostov, and Stavropol. Blessed with a mild climate and highly profitable agricultural sectors, these villages are wealthy, lively, and fully developed. [1]
Historic/Eco-Tourism Pockets: Villages along the Golden Ring, Karelia, or the Altai Mountains. These areas have preserved traditional wooden architecture and pristine nature but are supported by tourist revenue and infrastructure. [1, 2, 3]
2. The "Hardcore Survival" Zone (~40% – 50%)
This is the traditional, romanticized but physically demanding countryside. While visually stunning and peaceful, living here requires intense physical labor and self-reliance. [1]
Infrastructure Gaps: Rosstat data indicates that nearly 66% of rural Russian households lack centralized sewage (relying on outhouses or holding tanks), and roughly 30% lack paved, solid-surface roads connecting them to main highways. [1, 2, 3]
The Reality: Heating often relies on firewood or coal rather than pipeline gas, and water must be drawn from wells. For a summer vacation (dacha trip), it is highly therapeutic; for year-round living, it can be grueling. [1, 2, 3, 4]
3. The "Dying or Ghost Village" Zone (~20% – 25%)
This zone is entirely unsuited for a pleasant lifestyle due to severe economic and demographic collapse.
Depopulation: Since 1960, Russia's rural population has dropped by nearly half as young people migrate to cities. Out of roughly 153,000 rural settlements, almost 20,000 are completely abandoned ("ghost villages"), and tens of thousands of others have fewer than 10 elderly residents left.
Deep Periphery: Located in deep Siberian forests or the Far East, these villages suffer from closed schools, no local medical clinics, and grocery trucks that only visit once a week. [1, 2, 3, 4]

text:
Voor het klimaat moet alles wijken. Of toch niet?

Voor het klimaat moet Nederland meer doen. Sneller ook. Minder fossiele brandstoffen, minder uitstoot, industrie verduurzamen, woningen aanpassen. Voor natuur en stikstof worden eveneens miljarden uitgetrokken. Boeren stoppen, bedrijven krijgen hogere kosten en burgers betalen mee.

Het klimaat wacht immers niet.

Maar nog geen 2.000 kilometer verderop woedt een oorlog die inmiddels een enorme klimaat- en milieurekening heeft opgeleverd.

Volgens de laatste berekening heeft vier jaar oorlog in Oekraïne ongeveer 311 miljoen ton extra CO₂-equivalent veroorzaakt. Dat is ongeveer de jaarlijkse uitstoot van Frankrijk.

En CO₂ is nog maar een deel van het verhaal.

Bossen en natuurgebieden branden. Energiecentrales, olieopslagplaatsen, fabrieken en infrastructuur worden vernietigd. Brandstoffen, chemicaliën en andere vervuilende stoffen komen in bodem en water terecht. Landbouwgrond en ecosystemen raken beschadigd. Mijnen, explosieven, puin en militair afval blijven achter.

Daar komt de oorlogsproductie nog bij.

Granaten verschijnen niet vanzelf aan het front. Raketten, drones, tanks en ander materieel evenmin. Ze moeten worden gemaakt. Dat kost staal, grondstoffen, energie en transport. Voorraden worden aangevuld en vernietigd materieel wordt vervangen.

En straks moet er worden herbouwd. Woningen, wegen, bruggen, fabrieken en energievoorzieningen. Opnieuw beton, staal, energie en transport.

Zonder oorlog zou een belangrijk deel van deze extra uitstoot, productie, vernietiging en vervuiling er niet zijn.

In Nederland wordt ondertussen iedere ton CO₂ gewogen.

Geen fossiele brandstoffen gebruiken betekent minder klimaatbelasting. Logisch. Maar de redenering werkt ook andersom.

Geen oorlog betekent ook geen brandstof voor die tank, geen kerosine voor dat gevechtsvliegtuig, geen extra productie van die granaat, geen brandend oliecomplex en geen verwoeste fabriek die later opnieuw moet worden gebouwd.

Nederland en andere Europese landen blijven Oekraïne financieel en militair steunen.

Daar zijn redenen voor. Rusland viel Oekraïne aan. Veiligheid, soevereiniteit en de Europese veiligheidsorde wegen zwaar.

Maar daarmee wordt ook iets anders duidelijk.

Klimaat en natuur staan blijkbaar niet altijd bovenaan. Andere belangen kunnen zwaarder wegen.

Waarom lijkt die constatering zoveel moeilijker zodra het over beleid in eigen land gaat?

Van burgers worden hoge investeringen verlangd. Bedrijven moeten verduurzamen. Boeren stoppen vanwege natuur- en stikstofbeleid. Bij sommige beëindigingsregelingen gaat dat zelfs zo ver dat een deelnemer niet eenvoudig elders in de EU dezelfde veehouderijactiviteit kan voortzetten.

Kennelijk vinden we het daar wél belangrijk dat milieuwinst niet alleen op papier in Nederland ontstaat.

Maar de hoofdvraag is veel eenvoudiger.

Als veiligheid en geopolitiek zwaar genoeg kunnen wegen om enorme klimaat-, natuur- en milieuschade te accepteren, waarom wordt dan thuis zo weinig gesproken over het punt waarop andere belangen zwaarder mogen wegen?

Wanneer mag voedselproductie zwaarder wegen? Werkgelegenheid? Betaalbare energie? Een concurrerende industrie? Bestaanszekerheid?

Dat betekent niet dat Nederland Oekraïne moet laten vallen. En het betekent ook niet dat klimaat- of natuurbeleid moet stoppen.

Het betekent wel dat de belangenafweging kennelijk bestaat.

Dan mag die ook worden uitgelegd.

Aan de burger die zijn woning moet aanpassen. Aan de ondernemer die moet investeren. Aan de werknemer die ziet dat zijn bedrijf onder druk staat. En aan de boer die te horen krijgt dat natuur- en stikstofdoelen zulke vergaande consequenties noodzakelijk maken.

En die uitleg mag niet alleen van de regering en politiek komen.

Ook NGO's en klimaatactiegroepen als XR, die steeds verdergaande maatregelen verlangen, mogen deze vraag beantwoorden.

Hoeveel klimaat- en natuurschade mag worden geaccepteerd voor veiligheid en geopolitiek? En als het antwoord is dat andere belangen soms inderdaad zwaarder wegen, waarom geldt die redenering dan niet even zichtbaar wanneer de rekening bij Nederlandse burgers, boeren en bedrijven terechtkomt?

Misschien zijn daar goede antwoorden op.

Maar leg ze dan uit.

Want klimaat is mondiaal. CO₂ kent geen grenspaal. Vernietigde natuur wordt niet minder vernietigd omdat zij verderop in Europa ligt. Vervuild water wordt niet schoner omdat het niet door Nederland stroomt.

Als van burgers grote offers worden gevraagd voor klimaat en natuur, mogen zij ook vragen waarom die belangen de ene keer vrijwel onaantastbaar lijken en de andere keer moeten wijken voor iets wat belangrijker wordt gevonden.

Niet alleen de burger moet uitleggen wat hij voor klimaat en natuur doet. Politiek, regering en NGO's mogen ook uitleggen welke klimaat- en natuurschade zij bereid zijn te accepteren en waarom.

text:
A favor can arrive at exactly the right moment. A friend may help when you are struggling, a colleague may step in when work becomes overwhelming, or someone close to you may offer support without being asked. Most of the time, such gestures feel like kindness. They bring relief, gratitude, and a sense that someone cares.

But what happens after the favor is accepted?

Sometimes, the feeling of gratitude quietly turns into a sense of obligation. You may start wondering whether you owe that person something in return. Even when the other person never asks for anything, the memory of their help can influence your choices.

“To receive a favor is to sell one’s liberty.”

Kindness can bring relief, but accepting it can sometimes create an invisible debt.

Recently, France has faced challenges related to Islamic radicalism and tensions between Muslim communities and broader society, particularly in the context of violence and political integration. Reports indicate concerns about the influence of groups like the Muslim Brotherhood and incidents of antisemitism linked to these tensions. By 2022, 7 million immigrants lived in France, which is 10.3% of the total population. France faces complex challenges related to the reception and integration of these diverse populations. Whether they are asylum seekers, refugees, economic migrants, or undocumented, significantly influences their access to rights and services, with those in irregular situations often facing more severe inequalities due to their precarious status. There's a strain on social services. These problems are not only detrimental to migrants themselves but also have implications for French society as a whole, particularly in terms of social cohesion and economic potential. About 10% of the French population identifies as Muslim, with a significant portion being immigrants or descendants of immigrants from Muslim-majority countries. 48.2% of immigrants living in France were born in Africa.

From a broader historical viewpoint, for over 1,400 years, Islam has achieved remarkable expansion, winning the battle, the war—not chiefly through the free marketplace of ideas, but through a combination of conquest, structural incentives, high fertility, and cultural persistence, advancing under the false banner of religion while limiting genuine freedom of conscience.

The battle remains one of freedom: the right to believe, doubt, or change belief without coercion. Autocracies restrict liberty for power; Islam often does so under religious sanction, with the Quranic vision of ultimate dominion for Allah.

When Islam Prevails as the Victor: The Example of Iran

Iran after the 1979 Revolution offers a stark case study. Promises of liberation yielded theocratic control. Opposition was systematically eliminated, civilian firearms confiscated, and a morality police apparatus—including the Basij—empowered to enforce sharia. Women have faced punishment for minor dress violations; protests have repeatedly met lethal force. As recently as late 2025 and January 2026, widespread economic and freedom protests were crushed with live ammunition, mass arrests, internet blackouts, and hundreds to thousands of deaths, with the IRGC and Basij at the forefront. Public hangings from cranes, propaganda and surveillance maintain the regime’s narrative. What began with revolutionary hope solidified into authoritarian religious rule.

Conclusion

Let Iran stand as a warning to the world: it reveals what Islam has achieved historically through conquest and coercion, what it is capable of causing today, and what its’ classical doctrines envision for the future—unless it is firmly checked.

Should Islam even be recognized as a religion in the same category as others? Most faiths present their gods as offering moral guidance or counsel that individuals may accept or reject voluntarily. Islam, by contrast, demands total submission enforced through human intermediaries who administer sharia, collect jizya and zakat, punish apostasy, and subordinate all other ways of life. It is this inescapable human political element—fusing divine command with state power—that sets it apart and renders it less a voluntary faith than a comprehensive system of control.

Islam is at war with the world—not every individual Muslim (many of whom live quietly as moderates without power), but with the ideological framework itself when pursued in its classical, totalizing form. Islam, as a totalizing political-religious doctrine poses a unique threat to global stability and personal liberty wherever it gains unchecked influence.  It must be resisted, not with blanket hared of Muslims, but with clear-eyed defense of freedom, truth, and the open marketplace of ideas. The French political class unwittingly opened itself to a serious problem. The French citizens will be paying for it. Just ask the Persians in Iran.

Mark 2:23–28 / Matt 12:1–8 / Luke 6:1–5 - disciples plucking grain on the Sabbath and Jesus defends the actions with weak apologetics. Christians try to defend  with variations of it was a desperate situation but the fact that they were within walking distance of the local community to be discovered (within techum boundary) shows they had other options. His second argument, that the priesthood is allowed to "violate the sabbath" is also logically absurd.

Matt 5:31–32 forbidding divorce is objectively cruel and often amoral. If not for the myriad of messy cases of spousal disharmony, (eg physical abuse), the Mosaic Law's inclusion of divorce serves a vital function for war, enabling widows for whom their husbands bodies are not found or who's death lacked witnesses to remarry. 

Mark 7:14–23 permitting prohibited foods. etc.

Now I think you realized this because you circumscribed your claim to Jesus keeping the "moral law" perfectly. Of course let's not forget that the Sabbath is part of the moral law and is number 4 of the 10 "commandments". 

>that his Passover sacrifice fulfilled what the animal sacrifice pointed to, true atonement for sin and restoring right relationship with God

This makes little sense under light scrutiny. As you're well aware, there are different categories of offerings. There are guilt and sin offerings (Kodshei Kodashim), those are specifically for atonement from sin, correcting ones relationship with God, and they are eaten exclusively by the priests/cohanim.

This is nothing like the Passover offering which is eaten communally by the people not the priests (kodshei kalim), is time-bound and intimately tied to the holiday of Passover as a rememberance for the miracle of leaving Egypt, a holiday having little to do with sin (as opposed to Rosh HaShana or Yom Kippur). 

>Jesus is both Priest and Victim. As a Priest, he offered himself, and as a Victim he was slain as the bulls and lambs were slain.

Again the Messiah and Priest are separate institutions and there's no indication in the prophets that they are to join beyond some Picasso-esque homiletics(a la Psalms 110:4). On the contrary, the prophets very clearly indicate the continuation of the priesthood in the time of the messiah as distinct bodies, not converged into one: Jer 33:20-22 as we pointed out previously, but also ibid 17–18, 1 Chr 23:13, Mal 3:3–4, Ezek 40:46; 43:19; 44:15–16; 48:11

cf Ezek where the Nasi/King/Messiah is distinct and contributing, but not the priest: Ezek 44:3,45:16–17, 46:2, 12 (standing at the threshold, not participating in the worship), 45:22 -  brings an atonement for him and all the people not that he will be the priest and the atonement all rolled into one. 

This is what I mean by Rembrandt v. Picasso.

>And many of the other laws from the Mosaic covenant, like the dietary laws, Christians see as being part of the temporary, national laws that were in place to protect the nation of Israel, but no longer essential once the New Covenant was put into effect.

I think we've demonstrated above how these laws as part of the covenant are in fact immutable, but I will add this theological presumption borders on arrogance, albeit unwitting. The idea we can rationally understand the purpose of God's commandments and then deem them temporal and no longer needed is absurd. Solomon made similar errors despite his wisdom. He thought by understanding the rationale of not taking too many wives, acquiring horses, and accumulating wealth, they did not apply to him.

text:
Tom's Hardware wrote on 3 October about Amazon's new spending plan for the towns around its data centers.

Amazon calls the program Built Together. The company promised more than $1 billion over the next five years. AWS boss Matt Garman said communities would decide how the money gets used. He pointed at schooling, job training, energy and water bills, and whatever else a town picks for itself.

The education piece has the biggest headcount attached. Amazon wants to connect more than 300,000 students near its data centers to free associate degrees. It says it will cover whatever financial aid does not. The company also wants to fund training for up to 100,000 skilled trade workers a year. Those workers could then be hired by Amazon or by its construction partners.

The energy piece is easier to check. Amazon will give grants for heat pumps, insulation, water heaters, batteries and solar panels at schools, community buildings and homes. It aims to cut electricity costs by around 20% to 40% a year. It also aims to take up to $700 a year off a household bill.

Garman also called some of the complaints about data centers false and misleading. It lands at an awkward moment for the industry. Projects are being held up by data center bans, and polls show most Americans do not want one near their home. Other developers have already made offers. SpaceXAI offered people living nearby in Memphis and Southaven half off Starlink. Another developer said it will send $10,000 checks to 4,500 households if its 1,300 acre site gets approved.

One pair of numbers stuck with me. Amazon's commitment is more than $1 billion, spread over five years and across every data center town it builds in. At one site in Maryland, developers have proposed a $110 million package for a single community. That one site is close to a tenth of Amazon's whole five year figure.

text:
Iran-US tensions deepen as rial plunges and Hormuz remains closed

♦️ Iran’s rial sank to a new record low, with the dollar reaching around 2.69 million rials as the war and continuing US naval blockade put mounting pressure on Tehran’s economy.

♦️ The currency has now lost more than half its value over the past year, prompting state banks to sell up to $2 billion in an attempt to support the rial.

♦️ The economic strain is increasingly reaching ordinary Iranians, with inflation above 70% and households struggling with basic expenses and rent as the blockade constrains Iran’s vital oil exports.

♦️ Tehran partly blamed Washington for the currency turmoil, accusing US officials of promoting expectations that Iran’s economy is approaching collapse, while insisting the rial’s latest decline is temporary.

♦️ Washington, however, is signalling that the pressure will continue, with the US maintaining its naval blockade and Trump saying the economic campaign has achieved results beyond expectations.

♦️ The confrontation is now increasingly centred on the Strait of Hormuz, with parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf saying Iran will not reopen the strategic waterway until its seven conditions are implemented.

♦️ Iran had offered to reopen Hormuz under a broader deal involving a seven-day cessation of hostilities, the release of frozen Iranian assets, the lifting of restrictions on its oil exports and an end to the US naval blockade.

♦️ Trump rejected that proposal as Washington pushes for further nuclear concessions, while saying Iran has effectively abandoned plans for a nuclear weapon and that the war could end either through an agreement or military action.

♦️ Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said war and sanctions would not force Tehran to yield, stressing that Iran is ready for a diplomatic solution but would respond more forcefully to any new military attack.

♦️ With negotiations stalled, tensions are also spilling into diplomacy, as the US expelled two Iranian UN delegation members from New York, while Tehran says Washington has nevertheless continued sending new proposals through intermediaries.

text: Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, stationed at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma and III MEF, was taken into custody early Sunday by Okinawa Prefectural Police on suspicion of involvement in a robbery-murder. Authorities say Anna Yagi, 39, of Naha, was tragically killed at the Naminoue Crystal Hotel in Naha’s Wakasa district between roughly 2:10 a.m. and 4:15 a.m. Saturday, with her backpack and wallet stolen. Japanese reports reveal CCTV footage showing a man matching Ballard’s description entering with her and later leaving with her belongings; he was detained late Saturday in an entertainment district and has denied any wrongdoing. The U.S. Embassy in Tokyo and the Marine Corps are cooperating fully; the Corps confirms he remains in Japanese custody. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has issued a formal protest, condemning the incident as exceptionally brutal. Under the U.S.–Japan Status of Forces Agreement, Japan holds primary jurisdiction over off-duty crimes against Japanese civilians. Since the murder and robbery occurred in a civilian hotel and involve a local woman, they fall outside official-duty acts, giving Japan the legal authority to try the case. Washington can request a waiver, but such requests are rarely granted; in this case, Ballard faces a complex legal battle in a system that offers no plea bargains or guaranteed return to the U.S., leaving his future uncertain and the charges grave.

Hey doc it’s nice to see you again

“How have you been Mr. Sanders?”

Well,  to be honest I feel pretty crummy

“Uh oh, let’s go over your numbers. Well looks like your blood pressure is finally in check,  and all it took was a diuretic, ACE inhibitor, a Calcium channel blocker and an ARB to get you tuned up!  Oh and your A1C is doing ok at 6.1, ,  let’s just keep an eye on it and continue with the Metformin for now.  Ok great I see your LDL is at 80 mg/dl, looks like that Lipitor is doing the job.  Honestly your numbers look pretty good to me.”

But why do I feel so lousy then, could it be a side effect of all the medications? 

“Probably not, more likely it’s just that your getting older”

I’m only 37? 

“Well you’re not a spring chicken anymore and to be honest a whole lot of my patients your age feel pretty lousy too”

Really, maybe I am just getting old, what do you do with your other patients? 

“Well a lot of times they are just depressed and I’ll start them on some anti-depressants” 

How does that workout? 

“Not too sure but they seem to complain less” 

Interesting 

“Well Mr. Sanders why don’t I start you on some Zoloft?”

Ok, I guess….. thanks doc

But it became a problem for his career.

After Lagaan, Amin Hajee started rejecting roles because nothing seemed good enough compared to it.

Eventually, the offers dried up, and he found himself sitting at home.

That’s when his wife, Charlotte Whitby-Coles, stepped in.

She pushed him to start accepting work again instead of waiting endlessly for the perfect role.

Even when financial difficulties followed, she stood by him.

Then, when he decided to leave stable writing work to pursue his dream of directing, she supported him again mentally and financially.

He eventually made his directorial debut with Koi Jaane Na in 2021.

While it wasn’t a success, Hajee has openly acknowledged his failures and credited his wife for standing by him like a rock.

While Lagaan gave him recognition, Charlotte gave him the support to keep chasing his dreams.

text:
THE SALAMANDER OF LISIEUX VI
Sculpted above the group of the man with the griffin, we notice an enormous grimacing head adorned with a pointed beard. Its cheeks, ears, and forehead are stretched out to the extent that they take on the appearance of flaming expansions. This blazing mask, with an unfriendly grin, seems crowned and provided with horned, ribboned appendices which are resting on a twisted cord in the background of the cornice (Plate IX). With its horns and its crown, the solar symbol takes on the meaning of a genuine Baphomet; in other words, of the synthetic image in which Templar Initiates had assembled all the elements of high science and tradition. Truly a complex figure under its apparent simplicity, an eloquent figure, pregnant with teaching in spite of its rude and primitive aesthetic. If we recognize at first the mystic fusion of the natures of the Work, symbolized by the horns of the lunar crescent placed on the solar head, we are no less surprised by the strange expression, reflection of a devouring ardor emanating from the inhuman face, specter of the last judgment. Even the beard, hieroglyph of a luminous and fiery beam projected toward the earth, justifies the exact knowledge of our destiny that the scientist possessed.

Could we possibly be facing the dwelling of some affiliate of the sets of the Illuminati or of the Rosicrucians, descendants of the old Templars? The cyclical theory, concurrent with the doctrine of Hermes, is so clearly exposed here, that except for ignorance or dishonesty we could not suspect the knowledge of our Adept. As for us, our conviction is firm; we are certain not to be mistaken in front of so many categorical assertions: we indeed have before our eyes a baphomet, renewed from the one of the Templars. This image, about which we possess but vague indications or simple hypotheses, never was an idol, as some believed, but rather a complete emblem of the secret traditions of the Order, especially used outwardly as an esoteric paradigm, a seal of chivalry, and a sign of recognition. It was composed of an isosceles triangle, its apex pointed down, hieroglyph for water, first created element, according to Thales of Miletus, who maintained that "God is the Spirit which has formed all things from water" (1). A second similar triangle, inverted in relationship to the first, but smaller, was inscribed in its center and seemed to occupy the position reserved for the nose on the human face. It symbolized fire and more precisely, fire enclosed in water, or the divine spark, soul incarnate, life infused in matter. On the inverted base of the large triangle of water, there was a graphic sign similar to the Latin letter H or Greek [*158-1] (eta), but wider whose central bar was cut with a median circle. This sign in hermetic steganographiy indicates the universal Spirit, the Creative Spirit, God. Inside the large triangle, slightly above and on each side of the triangle of fire, one could see on the left the lunar circle with an inscribed crescent and on the right the solar circle with a visible center. These small circles were arranged in the manner of eyes. Finally, welded to the base of the small inner triangle, the cross, placed on the globe, thus realized the double hieroglyph of sulphur, active principle, associated to mercury, passive principle and solvent of all metals. A longer or shorter segment often located at the apex of the triangle was carved with lines of a vertical tendency where the layman could recognize not the expression of luminous radiation but a sort of goatee.

Thus presented, the baphomet assumed a gross animal form, imprecise and uneasy to identify. This would probably explain the diversity of descriptions it inspired, where the baphomet is seen as a haloed death head or a bucrane, sometimes the head of the Egyptian Hapi, of a goat, and, even better, the horrifying face of Satan himself! Simple impressions, far removed from reality, but images so unorthodox that they, alas, contributed to spread the accusation of demonology and sorcery upon the learned Knights Templar and became one of the foundations of their trial, one of the causes of their condemnation.

We have just seen what the baphomet was; now we must try to discover the meaning hidden behind this name.

In the pure hermetic expression corresponding to the labor of the Work, Baphomet comes from the Greek roots [*158-2] (Bapheus), dyer, and [*159-1], standing for [*159-2], the moon; unless we want to use [*159-3], [*159-4], in the genetive case, mother or matrix, which leads to the same lunar meaning, since the moon is truly the mother or the mercurial matrix which receives the tincture or seed of sulphur, representing the male, the dyer --- [*159-5] (Bapheus) --- in metallic generation. [*159-6] has the meaning of immersion and of tincture. And it can be said, without revealing too much, that sulphur, father and dyer of the stone, fertilizes the mercurial moon through immersion, which brings us back to the symbolic baptism of Mete, expressed again by the word baphomet (2). It appears as the complete hieroglyph of science, represented elsewhere in the personality of the god Pan, mythical image of nature in full activity.

The Latin word Bapheus, dyer, and the verb meto, to gather, collect, harvest, also indicate the special quality possessed by mercury or the moon of the sages, of collecting the tincture gradually as it emitted during the immersion or the king’s bath, and which the mother keeps in her bosom for the required time. It is the Grail containing the eucharistic wine, liquor of spiritual fire, vegetative liquor, living and vivifying, introduced into material things.

As for the origin of the Order, its lineage, the knowledge and beliefs of the Templars, we could not do better than to literally quote a fragment of the study which Pierre Dujols, the erudite and learned philosopher, devotes to the brother knights in his Bibliographie Generale des Sciences Occultes (3).

"The brothers of the Temple", says the author, "--- and we could no longer uphold the opposite view --- were truly affiliated to Manichaeism". Furthermore, Baron de Hammer’s thesis conforms to this opinion. For him, the sectarians of Mardeck, the Ismaelians, the Albigensians, the Templars, the Freemasons, the Illuminati, etc., depend on the same secret tradition emanating from this House of Wisdom (Dar-el-hickmet) founded by Hakem in Cairo around the 11th century. The German academician Nicolai concludes in the same sense and adds that the famous baphomet, which he derives from the Greek word [*159-7] (Baphometos), was a Pythagorean symbol. We will not spend any time with the divergent opinions of Anton, Herder, Munter, etc., but we will dwell for a moment on the etymology of the word baphomet. The idea of Nicolai is acceptable if we admit, with Hammer, this slight variation: [*160-1](Baphe Meteos), which could be translated as "baptism of Mete". Precisely a rite of this name has been established among the Ophites. Mete was an androgynous divinity representing naturing Nature. Proclus says verbatim that Metis, also called [*160-2] (Erikarpaios) or Germinating Nature, was the hermaphroditic god of the Snake worshippers. We also know that the Greeks venerated Prudence, designated by the word Metis, as Jupiter’s wife. In a word, this philological discussion indisputably confirms that the Baphomet was the pagan expression of Pan. And like the Templars, the Ophites had two baptisms: one, exoteric, the baptism of water, the other esoteric, that of the spirit, or fire. The latter was called the Baptism of Mete. St Justin and St Irenaeus called it illumination. It is the Freemasons’ baptism of Light. This purification --- the word is truly appropriate here --- is found on one of the Gnostic idols discovered by Monsieur de Hammer, which he illustrated. It holds in its lap --- mark well the gesture as it is very revealing --- a fire-filled basin. This fact, which should have struck the learned German and with him all of the symbolists, seems to have revealed nothing to them. And yet it is from this allegory that the famous myth of the Grail takes its origin. Indeed, the erudite baron talks abundantly about this mysterious vessel, whose exact meaning is still being sought. Everyone knows that in the ancient Germanic legend Titurel raises a temple to the Holy Grail at Montsalvat and entrusts its guard to twelve Knights Templar. Monsieur de Hammer would like to recognize in it the symbol of gnostic Wisdom, a very vague conclusion after having burned (4) for so long. Forgive us of we dare to suggest another point of view. The Grail --- who doubts it today? --- is the most elevated mystery of mystical Chivalry and of Masonry which degenerated from it; it is the veil of the Fire creator, the Deus absconditus (5) in the word INRI, engraved above Jesus’ head on the cross. When Titurel erected his mystical temple, it was to light the sacred fire of the Vestals, of the Mazadaens, and even of the Hebrews, for the Jews kept a perpetual fire in the temple of Jerusalem. The twelve custodians recall the twelve signs of the Zodiac annually crossed by the sun, a symbol of living fire. The vase of Baron de Hammer’s idol is identical with the pyrogenous vase of the Parsees, which is represented full of flames. The Egyptians also possessed this attribute: On the banks of the Nile, Serapis is often represented with the same object on his head, named Gardal. In this Gardal the priests kept the material fire, while the priestesses kept therein the celestial fire of Ptah. For the initiates of Isis, the Gardal was the hieroglyph of divine fire. And this Fire-god, this Love-God eternally incarnates into each being since everything in the universe contains his vital spark. It is the Lamb sacrificed since the beginning of the world, which the Catholic church offers to its faithful in the form of the Eucharist enclosed in the ciborium, like the Sacrament of Love. The ciborium --- honni soit qui mal y pense! (6) --- as well as the Grail and the sacred craters of all religions, represents the female reproductive organ and corresponds to the cosmogonic vessel of Plato, the cup of Hermes and Solomon, and the urn of the ancient Mysteries. The Gardal of the Egyptians is therefore the key of the Grail. It is, in short, the same word. Indeed, from distortion to distortion Gardal became Gradal, and then, with a sort of aspiration, Graal. The blood boiling in the holy chalice is the igneous fermentation of life or of the generating mixture. We can only deplore the blindness of those who are so obstinate as to only see in this symbol, stripped of its veils to the point of nudity, a profanation of the divine. The Bread and the Wine of the mystical Sacrifice are the spirit or the fire in matter, which, through their union, produce life. For this reason, all the Christian initiatic handbooks, called Gospels, cause Christ to say allegorically: "I am the Life; I am the living Brad; I have come to set things on fire, and surround him in the sweet exoteric sign of the ideal nourishment".

The Templars
The second great stream of Freemasonry finds its origins in the Templars, or Knights Templar as they were officially known. A military priesthood in the Catholic Church, the Templars were formally organized in 1118 by Hugh de Payens, their first Grand Master, who, following the Crusades, derived the name from the Temple of Jerusalem.

The Templars were the first religious community to yoke the cross to the sword. The Templars' initial stated purpose was to guard and guide pilgrims to the Holy City of Jerusalem. Gradually, the Templars' duties expanded to defend the Holy Land against all infidels and "any force menacing Jerusalem of their religion."

The nucleus of the Templars consisted of nine men. As the order grew, de Payens created 13 degrees within it.
Why he chose to stop at "thirteen" is not known. Perhaps it represented the tribes of Israel (eleven full tribes and the two half tribes of Joseph - Ephraim and Manasseh). Maybe it stood for the twelve disciples and Jesus Christ.

What is significant about the number "13" is that it identifies the Templar headquarters of our day.

Why Don’t We Have 13 Zodiac Signs Then?
Here’s where it gets interesting. The zodiac system we use today was developed by the Babylonians around 2,500 years ago. They divided the sky into 12 equal parts — one for each month of the year — and assigned a constellation to each section. Makes sense, right?

But here’s the problem: the sun actually passes through 13 constellations, not 12. The Babylonians knew about Ophiuchus, but they deliberately left it out to keep their tidy 12-sign system intact.

The NASA Announcement That Shook Everything
In 2016, NASA published a blog post explaining the science behind the zodiac, and mentioned — quite casually, I might add — that there’s actually a 13th constellation. The internet promptly lost its mind. Social media went into meltdown. People were having full-blown identity crises about their star signs!

NASA had to clarify (probably whilst rolling their eyes) that they study astronomy, not astrology, and they weren’t trying to change anyone’s zodiac sign. They were simply pointing out the astronomical facts.

But the damage was done. Ophiuchus had entered mainstream conversation.

So What Are the Dates for Ophiuchus Horoscope Sign?
If we were to include Ophiuchus in the zodiac system, it would occupy the dates from roughly 29th November to 17th December. Which means if you were born during this time and thought you were a Sagittarius all these years, you might technically be an Ophiuchus.

It took three months for the news of the "Boston Tea Party" to reach London, whereupon the British Parliament declared Massachusetts to be in a state of rebellion. Not realizing the significance of the Masonic division in the colonies, the Crown's action was swift and misguidedly drastic. The "Boston Port Bill," which placed an embargo on all trade with Boston, for example, effectively closed the port, and stiffened colonial resolve against the Crown.

The Congress was under the presidency of Templar Freemason Peyton Randolph, a prominent attorney and Provincial Grand Master of Virginia. Boston delegates included Samuel Adams and Paul Revere. In February 1775, the Massachusetts Provincial Congress met and announced plans for armed resistance. Within a month Templar Freemason Patrick Henry made his famous speech - "Give me liberty, or give me death" - to Virginia's Provincial Assembly. On April 18, 1775, 700 British troops were dispatched outside Boston. Templar Freemason Paul Revere made his famous ride, announcing "The Red Coats are coming!" Parties he said were paid by the superpowers offered projects in the Gaza Strip worth about $15 billion. An airport. A seaport. Economic work. Break the siege. CJP seriously needs to rethink its protest strategy. Announcing on October 2 that you will protest on October 10 is not pressure - it is an eight-day advance warning to the very state machinery you claim is determined to crush the movement.

Why give a hostile government and its police machinery eight days to prepare, deploy, intimidate, arrest, and neutralise a protest? This is not CJP’s first mobilisation. You have the network. You have the manpower. You have the organisational experience. If the objective is to create pressure, you should be able to mobilise within hours - not hand the government a calendar and ask it to get ready.

Your previous mass protest demanding Joker Pradhan’s resignation deserves credit, and his resignation showed that pressure works. But there was another uncomfortable reality that cannot be ignored: when the police came down on protesters, the leadership appeared considerably safer than the people who actually stood on the streets and took the risks. You cannot expect ordinary protesters to face arrests and police brutality while the leadership remains comfortably removed from the consequences of the mobilisation it called for.

And stop allowing the government to buy time with the usual promise that a “solution will be found soon.” If there is a solution, produce it. If there is no solution, continue the pressure. A protest should not be paused because the government has offered another vague assurance.

Take a lesson from Neha Bora. She has repeatedly demonstrated the kind of urgency, fearlessness and sharpness that street politics demands. Whether you agree with her or not, she often appears more ferocious and strategically decisive than an entire leadership structure with CJP’s resources.

You cannot fight a state machinery that is moving aggressively against you with a strategy that politely tells it when, where and how much time it has to prepare.

If the demand is serious, the mobilisation must be serious. Stop announcing protests like scheduled events. Create pressure before the government gets the chance to prepare for it.

text:
Law enforcement officers lose qualified immunity when a plaintiff proves both that the officer violated a “Constitutional Right” and that “The Right” was clearly established at the time of the incident.

How Qualified Immunity Fails in Court
Under the two-part test used by courts, an officer is denied protection if: 

•A constitutional violation occurred: 
The officer's conduct (such as using excessive force or conducting an unlawful search) violated the U.S. Constitution. 

•The law was clearly established: 
Existing precedent (from the U.S. Supreme Court, a federal appeals court, or a state supreme court) made it apparent and obvious to a reasonable officer that their specific conduct was unlawful. 

Scenarios Where Immunity Does Not Apply
Qualified immunity protects civil servants from personal monetary liability in civil lawsuits, but it does not apply in other contexts: 
•Criminal charges: 
Qualified immunity only shields officers from civil suits, meaning it offers no protection against criminal prosecution by state or federal authorities. 

•Municipal liability: 
The defense applies to individual officers, not to local government entities or cities themselves. 

•Injunctive relief: 
Plaintiffs seeking court orders to stop a specific police policy or practice rather than financial damages can bypass the doctrine

FYI : For anyone who doesn’t know what is meant by a “1983”
Section 1983 (codified at 42 U.S. Code § 1983) is a federal civil rights law that allows people to sue state and local government officials who violate their constitutional rights or federal laws while acting under government authority. 

Originally enacted as part of the Civil Rights Act of 1871 (also known as the Ku Klux Klan Act), the statute was designed during Reconstruction to protect newly freed individuals and combat lawlessness by public officials. 
Today, it serves as a primary legal tool to hold government actors accountable. 

How Section 1983 Works
•Does not create rights: 
Section 1983 does not grant new civil rights; instead, it provides a legal mechanism to enforce rights that already exist under the U.S. Constitution or federal statutes. 

•Under color of law: 
The defendant must have acted "under color of state law," meaning they used their official position, badge, or government authority to commit the wrongful act. 

•Proving a claim: 
A plaintiff must show that a state or local actor deprived them of a federal right and that this violation caused actual harm or injury. 

Common Examples of Claims
•Police misconduct: 
Cases involving excessive force, police brutality, wrongful arrest, or false imprisonment. 

•Jail and prison conditions: 
Situations where correctional staff show "deliberate indifference" to an inmate's serious medical needs or safety. 

•Constitutional violations: 
Infringements on free speech, religious freedom, or due process protections guaranteed by the First, Fourth, and Fourteenth Amendments. 

Available Remedies
•Damages: 
Financial compensation for medical bills, lost wages, pain and suffering, or wrongful death.

•Injunctive relief: 
Court orders requiring a government agency or official to change a policy or stop specific misconduct.

•Attorney's fees: 
Compensation to help cover the legal costs of bringing the lawsuit

Law enforcement officers lose qualified immunity when a plaintiff proves both that the officer violated a “Constitutional Right” and that “The Right” was clearly established at the time of the incident.

How Qualified Immunity Fails in Court
Under the two-part test used by courts, an officer is denied protection if: 

•A constitutional violation occurred: 
The officer's conduct (such as using excessive force or conducting an unlawful search) violated the U.S. Constitution. 

•The law was clearly established: 
Existing precedent (from the U.S. Supreme Court, a federal appeals court, or a state supreme court) made it apparent and obvious to a reasonable officer that their specific conduct was unlawful. 

Scenarios Where Immunity Does Not Apply
Qualified immunity protects civil servants from personal monetary liability in civil lawsuits, but it does not apply in other contexts: 
•Criminal charges: 
Qualified immunity only shields officers from civil suits, meaning it offers no protection against criminal prosecution by state or federal authorities. 

•Municipal liability: 
The defense applies to individual officers, not to local government entities or cities themselves. 

•Injunctive relief: 
Plaintiffs seeking court orders to stop a specific police policy or practice rather than financial damages can bypass the doctrine

FYI : For anyone who doesn’t know what is meant by a “1983”
Section 1983 (codified at 42 U.S. Code § 1983) is a federal civil rights law that allows people to sue state and local government officials who violate their constitutional rights or federal laws while acting under government authority. 

Originally enacted as part of the Civil Rights Act of 1871 (also known as the Ku Klux Klan Act), the statute was designed during Reconstruction to protect newly freed individuals and combat lawlessness by public officials. 
Today, it serves as a primary legal tool to hold government actors accountable. 

How Section 1983 Works
•Does not create rights: 
Section 1983 does not grant new civil rights; instead, it provides a legal mechanism to enforce rights that already exist under the U.S. Constitution or federal statutes. 

•Under color of law: 
The defendant must have acted "under color of state law," meaning they used their official position, badge, or government authority to commit the wrongful act. 

•Proving a claim: 
A plaintiff must show that a state or local actor deprived them of a federal right and that this violation caused actual harm or injury. 

Common Examples of Claims
•Police misconduct: 
Cases involving excessive force, police brutality, wrongful arrest, or false imprisonment. 

•Jail and prison conditions: 
Situations where correctional staff show "deliberate indifference" to an inmate's serious medical needs or safety. 

•Constitutional violations: 
Infringements on free speech, religious freedom, or due process protections guaranteed by the First, Fourth, and Fourteenth Amendments. 

Available Remedies
•Damages: 
Financial compensation for medical bills, lost wages, pain and suffering, or wrongful death.

•Injunctive relief: 
Court orders requiring a government agency or official to change a policy or stop specific misconduct.

•Attorney's fees: 
Compensation to help cover the legal costs of bringing the lawsuit

text:
For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith—and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God.

Over Yosemite Valley, California, USA.

Paul wrote to believers in Ephesus who knew what it felt like to measure themselves against a scoreboard. Effort. Reputation. Religious performance. Then he told them the better news: salvation is not a paycheck you earn. It is grace—God’s free gift—received through faith. The story does not end with exhausted people still trying to climb high enough. It ends with open hands. Hearts that stop striving long enough to receive what love already offered. Dead places made alive. A gift that cannot be bought and does not need to be repaid with fear.

That same gift still meets ordinary mornings. When you feel behind. When shame whispers that you must prove yourself before you are welcome. When rest feels undeserved. Grace does not wait for a perfect resume. It finds you as you are, then lifts you—not by your grip, but by His.

Today, receive what you cannot manufacture. Let the gift quiet the inner ledger. Speak gentler to yourself and to the person beside you. Share patience the way it was shared with you. Live from the relief of being given what you could never earn—and let that relief become kindness that travels farther than pride ever could.

Towards a bloody disaster 

Why Did the Negotiations Between PTI and the Ruling Coalition Collapse, and What Could Be Their Disastrous Consequences?
If terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is considered the most pressing issue, why did the talks collapse despite agreement on the contentious points concerning terrorism?
What is surprising is that, according to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, PTI and its provincial government had accepted all the federal government's demands regarding terrorism. Similarly, according to PPP leader Sherry Rehman, an agreement on the fight against terrorism had been reached on four occasions. On the other hand, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja summed up his party’s position as such: 
“anti-terorrism actions in KPK would be based on agreement between the federal government and the KPK government and would be framed on the basis of consultation with, and the buy-in of, the different political parties represented in the KPK assembly … we have zero tolerance for terrorism and are committed to rooting it out. We are against so-called collateral damage in the form of innocent lives and internal displacement of the local population. Policies and actions aimed at fighting terror must have the support of the local population and be based on ground intelligence. The wisdom provided by the jirga held in the KPK assembly of all the political and tribal notables of the province, including the merged districts, must be heeded. This was not acceptable to the federal government.” 
Then what was the dispute really about?
Primarily, Federal govt wants a free hand for Pak Army to continue with its kinetic operations, which are not endorsed by local communities. Hence, the deadlock. 
No less importantly was about access to Imran Khan and his legal rights as a prisoner—rights whose enforcement has been ordered by the Supreme Court, but whose implementation is being obstructed by the federal and Punjab provincial governments in violation of the Court's orders.
Thus, Imran Khan has emerged as the root cause of the entire confrontation, as neither the government nor its patrons are prepared to grant him even his legitimate and lawful rights.
Even if the political operators were willing to offer some political concessions, the powers that be remained determined to ruthlessly crush every form of resistance or non-compliance. 
Now, the drums of confrontation are beating on both sides.
The Corps Commanders' statement had expressed an unequivocal determination to crush, with full force and without discrimination, any demonstrations resembling those of May 9.
Meanwhile, Chief Minister Sohail Afridi has embarked today, October 4, on a prolonged long march, which will head towards Islamabad after October 7, when the capital will have remained under lockdown for two weeks.
There are still three or four days in between.
Can a middle ground for reconciliation still be found? But who will reason with those who fancy themselves gods?

(An invocation to ward off impending calamity!)

text:
Zelensky keeps hitting diesel. November is the target.
Trump asked on 13 September to stop knocking out Russian diesel. Not a hint. A public request, repeated days later, with the word diesel all over the call. On 3 October Kyiv answered by promising more refineries. Samara and Volgograd had already burned the night before. The announcement came after the strike.
That is not a war running on inertia. US diesel was over $6.50 a gallon by late September, gasoline near $4.50, and the midterms sit a few weeks out. Voters punish the party in power for the pump. The White House has spent a month saying the refinery campaign is what hurts the world. Kyiv heard that and booked another round.
The ceasefire offer from 22 September does not rescue this. Ready for any format, but no one-sided stop, and only if Moscow leaves the Ukrainian grid alone. Fine sentence for the cameras at the UN. Trump had already claimed both sides agreed on 14 September. The truce died the next day. Three weeks later the same president tells Reuters the documents are in, the doctrine is new, and the reply is oil refiners, because that is what pays for the war. Documents nobody else has seen. A doctrine announced after the drones had already flown.
Call it self-defense and the price still lands in Ohio, not in the Donbas. Call it reciprocity and the reciprocity was the thing he just shelved. The economies he still asks for money, air defense and winter cover are the same economies now paying six and a half dollars for the fuel that moves their food. A leader who needs those economies does not set their diesel on fire in October unless October is the point.
The climate line is the ugly extra. Refinery fires, a war that does not pause, and a winter campaign he says is designed to empty his own cities. His people take the grid strikes. His donors take the invoice. Trump takes the midterms. That is a strange order of priorities for a man who says he is only answering Moscow.
One number sits there for anyone who wants it: Middle East diesel losses from March to August ran near 770,000 barrels a day, the Russian drop near 350,000. The Gulf still explains more of the shortage than Kyiv does. So why, if the price shock is mostly not his, does he refuse the one strike Trump begged him to drop?
If this is not a shot at November, what is the date on the ceasefire?

NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte has urged member states to blame any incident they find suspicious on Russia even if they lack irrefutable evidence. He also hailed a recent accusation made by Estonia against its eastern neighbor and called on other nations to follow suit.
Speaking at a joint press conference with Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius this week, Rutte encouraged a public blame game over what he called “malign grey zone activities” routinely attributed to Russia by NATO members.
“You have heard the Supreme Allied Commander yesterday saying, ‘Hey, when able, when you are sure it is the Russians, or almost sure it is the Russians, attribute it to the Russians’ – exactly like Estonia did today. I applaud it,” Rutte said.
On Monday, NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe Alexus Grynkewich described publicly attributing these types of incidents to Russia as a “deterrent” against the supposed “Russian threat” during remarks before a European Parliament committee.
Rutte has been known for his staunch anti-Russian position, as well as his ardent support for Kiev in the conflict with Moscow.
